120 g dark chocolate, chopped and melted
st: Heat the cream in a saucepan. When just starting to simmer, add the dark chocolate. Stir until melted, remove from the heat and stir to form a smooth ganache.
Spoon the ganache onto half the biscuits and drizzle the white chocolate onto the remaining biscuits.
Top the biscuits with the toasted nuts and berries and allow to set.

ing: sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
st: Peel the stalks of the artichokes and neaten the ends. Soak in salted water for 30 minutes.

Drain the artichokes and pack into a saucepan with the lemon, garlic and peppercorns. Pour over the oil and enough water to cover. Place a small plate and a weight on top to keep them submerged during cooking.

Cover and simmer for 40 minutes or until tender. Test the stalks â they should be tender when pierced. Drain well. Serve with the Parmesan mayonnaise for dipping the fleshy leaves and stalks, discarding the chokes.

ing: 1 large bulb Fennel, trimmed and chopped
1.5 kg Tightly closed mussels in the shell
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
300 g Red skinned potatoes, peeled and chopped
st: Clean the mussels using a small sharp knife, or get the fishmonger to do it for you. Soak the tightly closed mussels in iced water for 1 hour. Discard any mussels that are not tightly closed.

Place the mussels in a large, heavy saucepan and add the wine and a few fennel fronds. Cover tightly and turn up the heat. Leave for a few minutes, then check to see whether the mussels have opened. Remove them from the pan as they open, leaving any unopened ones in the pan. Give them a chance to open but discard any that remain stubbornly closed. Set aside the mussels and strain the liquor. It should be about 1 cup.

Gently cook the chopped fennel in the olive oil and butter until very soft but still pale. Stir in the garlic and potatoes. Pour in the reserved liquor and stock and simmer, covered, for 20 minutes or until the potatoes are tender.
Set aside Â¼ of the mussels in the shell for garnishing. Remove the remaining mussels from their shells.

Blend the soup, adding half the shelled mussels, plus any extra liquor. Stir in the remaining shelled mussels and the cream. It shouldnât need salt but a grinding of pepper would be good. Once cooled, chill. Chill the reserved mussels in the shell for garnishing.

To serve, thin down the soup with more stock if necessary. Check the seasoning and garnish with the mussels in the shell and a few torn fennel fronds. If you like, add a drizzle of cream to each serving.

Preheat the oven to 180Â°C. Pour the verjuice into a shallow pan and bring to a simmer. Spread a large sheet of clingwrap on a work surface. Blanch the vine leaves by dipping each one in the verjuice for 10 seconds. Spread on the clingwrap to dry.

Add the honey and thyme to the verjuice, then lay the grapes in the pan on their sides. Poach gently for about 7 minutes, turning often, or until the skin is splitting and fruit is just beginning to collapse. Remove the grapes from the pan and set aside to drain in a colander.
Turn up the heat and boil the verjuice until it has reduced by half and is slightly thickened and glossy. Set aside.

Cut a cross into the top of the Camembert and push a few thyme leaves into the incisions. Wrap the cheese in the blanched vine leaves, then set it on a sheet of baking paper. Wrap to form a loose parcel and secure with string. Place on a baking sheet and bake at 180Â°C for 7â10 minutes, or until the cheese feels very soft and oozy.
Remove the baking paper and place the cheese on a platter with the poached grapes. Drizzle the verjuice syrup over the grapes and serve immediately with crisp golden croutons or Melba toast.

t: Chicken with roast onions and verjuice
ing: 1 bunch Green grapes, stripped from their stems
1 bunch Red grapes, stripped from their stems
sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
st: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C. Cover the onions with boiling water and set aside for 15 minutes (this loosens their skins).

In the meantime, heat the oil in a large shallow pan and fry the chicken, in batches and skin-side down, over a medium-high heat until the skin is crisp and a beautiful golden brown. (Donât turn the pieces over or let them cook through.) Set aside on a plate.

Cut each blanched onion in half lengthways, trim the tops and bottoms, and slip off the skins. Fry, cut side down, in the hot chicken fat left in the pan, for 3 minutes, or until nicely caramelised. Take care not to burn them. Carefully turn the onions over using tongs and fry for a further 3 minutes. Remove using a slotted spoon and set aside on a plate.
Add the bay leaves, thyme and garlic to the pan and cook over a low heat for 1 minute, without allowing the garlic to brown.

Deglaze the pan with the verjuice and wine, stirring and scraping to loosen the golden sediment on the bottom of the pan. Tip any juices that have accumulated under the chicken into the pan. Simmer over a brisk heat for 2 minutes to burn off the alcohol.

Arrange the chicken pieces and onions in a roasting tray, and tuck in the grapes. Pour the hot wine/verjuice mixture around the chicken, and scatter over the bay leaves and thyme sprigs. Season to taste.
Bake for 40 minutes, or until the chicken is cooked through and the grapes are beginning to collapse.
Serve immediately with a crisp green salad and crusty bread to mop up the juices.
Bring a saucepan of water to a gentle simmer. Roughly chop the chocolate and place in a metal or glass bowl over the simmering water, taking care not to allow the bowl to touch the water.
Dip the grapes into the melted chocolate and place on baking paper to set.
Serve the grapes with the chocolate covered cream cheese.

ing: sea salt and feshly ground pepper
Baby butter lettuce leaves, to serve
1 small bulb Fennel, thinly sliced and crisped in ice water
sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
A handful torn fresh mint leaves
sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
8  pieces Free range chicken drumsticks and thighs
st: Preheat the oven to 200ÂºC.

Wash and dry the chicken. Season and place in an oiled roasting pan. Pour over the verjuice. Drizzle with olive oil and bake, one shelf above the middle, for 30 minutes or until nicely browned and tender.
To serve, moisten the chicken with pan juices and spoon over the salsa. Serve with salad leaves to catch the juices.
Preheat the oven to 180Â°C.
Cut the nectarines in half and remove the stones. Arrange in a baking dish lined with baking paper.
Place a disc of cream cheese on each nectarine half, then pour some maple syrup over. Stud the cheese with a few berries and scatter the rest around the nectarines.
Bake for 10 to 15 minutes or until the fruit is tender and the cheese is soft and melted.
Spoon the pan juices over and serve warm or cold.
Preheat the oven to 200Â°C.
In a saucepan over a medium to high heat, bring the nectarine and apple juice to the boil and cook until the fruit is soft.
Transfer to a blender and blend until smooth. Add a pinch of salt and white sugar, to taste, then rub through a sieve and chill.
Meanwhile, whisk the egg whites until stiff peaks form. Add the caster sugar, one tablespoon at a time, whisking to dissolve each spoon of sugar before adding the next.
Using a sharp knife, remove the centre of the Madeira loaf, then fill with Caramel Swirl ice cream.
Spoon the meringue mixture on top and bake for 4 to 5 minutes, or until the meringue is golden in colour.
Cut into thick slices and serve immediately in bowls of chilled nectarine soup.

ing: sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
st: Heat the canola oil in a pan over a high heat. Coat the fillet in the crushed peppercorns and salt, then sear in the hot pan until the fillet is just browned, no more than 1 minute.
Allow the fillet to rest for 5 minutes, then wrap tightly in clingwrap and chill for 1 hour.
Mix together all the ingredients and drizzle with dressing just before eating.

ing: sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
st: Preheat the oven to 200Â°C.
Divide the dough into four pieces. Click here for our basic pizza dough recipe.
Sprinkle the counter with flour and roll out into rectangles.
Top with the Taleggio cheese (or Gouda), tomato and garlic and put on a greased baking tray.
Bake for 15 minutes, or until golden and cooked through.
Mix the basil leaves, nectarines, olive oil, lemon juice and salt and pepper.
Spoon onto the pizza and serve.

ing: 240 g Self-raising flour, plus extra for dusting
st: Place the flour, butter, vanilla seeds and a pinch of salt in a mixing bowl and mix well. Add water, a little at a time, stirring the mixture with a fork to form a pliable dough.
Turn out onto a floured surface and knead for 3 to 5 minutes, or until the dough becomes "loose". Set aside to rest. Chop the berries and mix with the walnut and a pinch of salt.
Divide the dough into 12 balls and roll out into discs. Place a spoonful of walnut-berry mixture into the middle of each disc, fold over the sides, and press the ends together to seal.
To a saucepan over a medium heat, add the water, sugar and lemon peel and bring to a light simmer. Add the dumplings and simmer, covered, for 10 to 15 minutes, or until cooked.
Serve the dumplings with the warm stewed berries and a generous helping of lightly whipped cream.
Dry fry the almonds in a pan over a medium heat until golden brown. Remove from the pan.
Whisk together the eggs, milk, vanilla paste and salt until smooth. Melt half the butter in a pan over medium heat.
Soak the bread in the egg mixture until completely coated, then cook in 2 batches on each side until golden brown.
Heat the blueberries, sugar and lemon juice in a small frying pan for 5 minutes.
Spread 4 slices of the bread with lemon curd, top with the blueberry mixture, then the remaining bread.
Slice, scatter over the toasted almonds and dust with icing sugar before serving.

ing: 250 g Hazelnuts, toasted and finely ground
st: Preheat the oven to 160Â°C.
Cream the butter and caster sugar together until pale and fluffy. Beat in the eggs, one at a time, until incorporated.
Split the vanilla pod and, using the tip of a sharp knife, scrape out the seeds and fold into the creamy egg mixture, along with the polenta, ground hazelnuts, baking powder, lemon juice and zest.
Grease and line a 23 cm baking tin, then spread the blueberries onto the base and sprinkle with the brown sugar. Pour in the cake mixture and bake for 1 hour or until a skewer comes out clean.

Set aside for at least 1 hour in order to cool before removing from the tin. Place a plate onto the top of the cake, then quickly flip over and remove the cake from the tin. Serve with dollops of clotted cream, if desired.

ing: 2 large granny smith apple, sliced into 3 discs
st: Create little towers with the apple, peanut butter, crushed rusks and raisins.
Other great toppings include toasted coconut, chocolate chips, flaked almonds and chopped dried fruit.
Serve immediately.
Beat the egg white until stiff peaks form.
Dip the violets into the egg white to coat, then scatter liberally with caster sugar. Place on wax paper or a silicon mat to set.
Dip the edges of the figs into the melted chocolate and arrange on a silicon mat to set.
In shallow bowls, top spoonfuls of mascarpone with the sugared violets and figs and serve with rose-petal jam and kumquats.
Sign in/Register
Rinse the baby beetroot and place in a saucepan of water, bring to the boil and cook for 15 to 20 minutes, or until tender. Drain, peel and cut into small chunks.
Leave to cool slightly, then combine with the yoghurt, a squeeze of lemon juice and seasoning, to taste.
Spoon over the crisp watercress, top with a few pomegranate rubies and serve as a side to spicy kebabs and naan bread.

ing: 3/4 cup Fresh mint leaves, leaves picked from stalks
2 Mangoes, peeled and cut into wedges
2 x 40 g tubs Simply toasted coconut
1 cucumbers, cut into thin ribbon slices (use a peeler)
sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
st: Brush the steaks with olive oil and season them well with salt and black pepper.
Heat a griddle or frying pan and cook the steaks for a few minutes on each side or until cooked to your liking. Set them aside to rest.
Put all the salad ingredients in a bowl.
For the coconut and ginger dressing, mix all the ingredients together.
Cut the steaks into thick slices, place them on the salad and drizzle with the salad dressing.

ing: 2 stalks Fresh lemongrass, cut into 4 cm long pieces
750 g Skinless, boneless chicken thighs, cut into 3 cm cubes
250 g Exotic mushrooms, stemmed, caps cut into bite-size pieces
3 x 3  cm piece Fresh ginger, peeled
st: Using the back of a knife, lightly bruise the lemongrass and ginger.
Bring the lemongrass, ginger, lime zest, juice and chicken stock to the boil in a large saucepan.
Reduce the heat and simmer for 8 â 10 minutes until the flavours have blended.
Strain the mixture into a clean saucepan and discard the solids.
Add the chicken pieces and bring the mixture back to the boil.
Reduce the heat, add the mushrooms and simmer for 15 â 20 minutes, skimming occasionally, until the chicken is cooked through and the mushrooms are tender.
Mix in the coconut milk, fish sauce and sugar.
Divide the soup between 6 serving bowls and serve with a drizzle of chilli oil, fresh coriander leaves and lime wedges.
Combine all the ingredients in a blender and process until the ice has broken up into a âslushieâ consistency.
Fill glasses with ice cubes and top with the slushie.
Garnish with fresh mint leaves.

t: Coconut, soya and chilli prawn skewers
ing: 750 g Prawns, peeled, deveined, tails left intact
st: Combine the coconut milk, coriander, garlic, chilli, fish sauce, soya sauce and lime zest in a shallow dish and reserve 2 tablespoons of the marinade for basting.
Add the prawns to the remaining marinade and toss to coat.
Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for 1 hour.
Heat a braai or chargrill on a medium-high heat.
Add the tablespoon of lime juice to the chilled prawn marinade and toss to coat.
Thread the prawns onto skewers and grill for 2 â 3 minutes on each side, brushing them with the reserved marinade, until pink and lightly charred.

ing: 2 x 40 g tubs Simply toasted coconut
st: Preheat the oven to 170 Â°C.
Lightly grease and line the bases of 3 x 20 cm cake tins.
For the sponge, use an electric mixer to whisk the butter (340 g) and castor sugar (375 g) until light and pale.
Very gradually, beat in the eggs, mixing well after each addition.

Sift the flour (340 g) and baking powder (1/3 tsp) into the mixture and fold in the coconut (110 g) until thoroughly incorporated. If the mixture seems too thick, add a few spoons of milk. Lastly, fold in the lime zest and juice (4 1/2 limes).
Divide the mixture evenly between the 3 tins. Level it out with a palette knife and bake in the oven for 20 minutes or until springy and cooked through.
Allow the cakes to cool slightly, then remove them from the tins and leave to cool completely.

For the icing, beat the butter (200 g), cream cheese (250 g), coconut (3 Tbsp) and vanilla (1/2 tsp) until smooth, then gradually beat in the icing sugar (400 g) until well incorporated. Lastly, mix in the lime zest and juice (2 limes).

To assemble the cake, spread some of the icing on top of the base cake layer then top with the next cake layer and repeat with remaining layers. Cover the whole cake with the rest of the icing and smooth with a palette knife.
Gently press the toasted coconut (2 x 40 g tubs) onto the sides of the cake and top with a sprinkling of lime zest (2 limes).

ing: 4 Cardamom pods, seeds crushed and pods discarded
approx. 500 g Mangoes, peeled and thinly sliced
approx. 600 g whole mangoes for Fresh mango pulp
2 Tbsp Coconut oil, plus extra for greasing
st: Preheat the oven to 180 Â°C.
Grease a 23 cm diameter tart tin with coconut oil.

For the crust, mix all the ingredients (2 Tbsp coconut oil, 300 g ground almonds, 150 g desiccated coconut and 5 Tbsp maple syrup) in a food processor until just combined. Add 1 â 2 tablespoons of water if the dough is very dry. Chill for half an hour.
Press the chilled dough into the tart tin to form an even crust. Chill in the freezer for 10 â 15 minutes.
Line the tart crust with baking paper and fill with baking beans. Bake blind for 20 â 25 minutes until the edges have lightly browned. Allow to cool.
For the filling, purÃ©e the mango pulp (400 ml), maple syrup (2 Tbsp), lime zest (2 limes) and cardamom (4 pods).

Place 1/4 of this mixture in a heatproof bowl and sprinkle the gelatine over it. Place the bowl over a pan of simmering water and whisk until the gelatine has completely dissolved. Mix it with the rest of the purÃ©e and set aside.
Whip the cream until stiff peaks are formed.
Gently fold the mango purÃ©e into the cream.
Place the bowl of mango filling in the freezer for 45 minutes, stirring occasionally. The filling should thicken.
Spoon the filling into the baked tart shell and chill for at least 5 hours.
To serve, top with sliced mango (approx. 500 g).

ing: 500 g Boneless, skinless chicken breasts, thinly sliced into strips
approx.24 Skewers, soaked in cold water for 20 minutes
4 carrots, cut into thin ribbon strips (use a peeler)
st: For the pickled carrot, place the vinegar, sugar and water in a saucepan over a medium heat. Stir for 2 minutes or until the sugar has dissolved.
Transfer to a heatproof bowl, add the carrot ribbons and stir to combine.
Set aside to cool completely, then stir in the dill.
For the peanut and coconut sauce, bring the coconut milk to a simmer in a small saucepan.
Whisk in the curry paste for about 1 â 2 minutes until it has dissolved.
Whisk in the peanut butter, chicken stock and brown sugar.
Reduce the heat and cook, stirring constantly for about 5 minutes until the sauce is smooth.
Remove from the heat and add the lime juice and salt. Set aside to cool to room temperature.
Thread the chicken onto skewers and brush lightly with olive oil.
Preheat a grill or grill pan to a medium-high heat and sear or grill the chicken for about 5 â 7 minutes in batches, only turning once, until cooked through.
Serve the grilled chicken warm with the spicy peanut and coconut sauce for dipping and the pickled carrots on the side.

ing: 3 cups Fresh mango (or oranges), peeled and sliced
3 cups Pineapple, peeled, core removed and chopped
st: Place all the ingredients in a blender and blend until smooth.
To serve, pour into 6 glasses and garnish with mint leaves.
If preferred, chill for an hour before serving.

t: Coconut, rose and raspberry ice cream
st: Blend the raspberries in a food processor and set aside.
Gently heat the maple syrup, coconut cream, double cream, rose water and white chocolate in a saucepan until combined and the chocolate has melted.
Transfer the mixture to a heatproof bowl and place the bowl over a saucepan of gently simmering water, making sure the base of the bowl does not touch the water.
Add the eggs and egg yolks to the mixture and cook, stirring constantly for about 10 minutes, until it lightly coats the back of a spoon. Allow to cool.
Transfer the mixture to a freezer-proof lidded container and freeze for 1 â 2 hours until slushy and frozen around the edges.
Remove from the freezer and blend in a food processor, then pour back into the freezer-proof container.
Pour the raspberry purÃ©e on top of the ice cream mixture and swirl it around with a spoon.
Close the freezer-proof container and freeze the ice cream until firm.

ing: 6 x 150 g Salmon fillets, skin left on
90 g Fresh mint, large stalks removed
90 g Fresh coriander, large stalks removed
st: For the sauce, place the herbs, ginger, garlic, fish sauce, lime juice and chilli in a food processor and blend to form a paste.
Slowly add the coconut milk to create a vibrant green sauce.
Heat a frying pan and add a splash of oil.
When very hot, add the salmon fillets skin side down, and cook for about 4 minutes. Turn the fillets and cook for a further 4 â 6 minutes until golden and crispy.
Transfer the sauce to a pan and heat through.
Serve the salmon with lime wedges and the warmed sauce and udon noodles, topped with the toasted coconut shavings and fresh mint leaves.
Place the sugar in a small saucepan over a medium heat and whisk until dissolved. Once the sugar has turned golden, add the almonds, toss to coat, then turn out onto silicone baking paper to cool.
Pour the chocolate onto a silicone baking mat in a baking tray. Top with the marshmallows, coconut and popcorn. Crush the almonds and scatter over.
Chill to set and break into shards to serve.

ing: 25 g 70% dark chocolate, chopped and melted
st: Beat all the ingredients together, then chill until set.
Generously spread onto toasted sourdough, croissants, flapjacks or pancakes.

ing: 120 g dark chocolate, chopped and melted
st: Beat the cream until stiff peaks form, then chill until required.
Place the egg yolks, coffee, 2 tbsp sugar and the salt into a glass bowl. Place the bowl over a pot of simmering water and cook, whisking continually, until doubled in volume, about 3 minutes.
Remove from the heat, add the chocolate and stir to combine. Beat the egg whites with the remaining sugar. Fold the egg whites into the whipped cream, then gently fold into the chocolate mixture.
Place in a serving bowl and chill for 1â2 hours, or until set.
Preheat the oven to 160Â°C and grease a 20 x 20 cm baking tray.
Using an electric beater, beat the egg whites until stiff peaks form, then set aside.
Whisk the egg yolks, vanilla extract and sugar until light and creamy. Add the melted butter and continue whisking until well incorporated.
Fold the flour and cocoa into the egg yolk mixture using a spatula. Gradually fold in the warmed coconut milk and milk.
Gently fold in the egg whites, a third at a time.
Pour the mixture into a greased baking tray and bake for 50â60 minutes. Allow to cool, then chill for 1 hour.

ing: 230g unsalted butter, cold and cut into small cubes
560 g cake flour, plus extra for dusting
st: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C and grease4 x 22 cm cake tins.
Sift the flour,bicarbonate of soda and salt into a bowl.Using an electric beater, cream the butterand sugar until light and fluffy.
Add theeggs, vanilla and buttermilk to the sugarmixture and beat until well incorporated.Mix in the chocolate and coffee.
Gentlyfold in the dry ingredients and pour intothe cake tins. Bake for 30 minutes, then setaside to cool.

To make the buttercreamicing, cream the butter, 1 cupicing sugar and a small amount of themilk until light and fluffy using an electricbeater. Gradually add the remaining icingsugar and milk, alternating betweenthe two, until combined. Divide thebuttercream between 3 bowls and foldthe each chocolate into one of the bowls.Chill until required.
To make the fudgyicing, mix the chocolate and condensedmilk until glossy.
To make the Rice Krispieclusters, fold the Rice Krispies into themelted chocolate and spoon onto bakingpaper. Chill to set.
To assemble the cake,use the buttercream icing to sandwichtogether the cakes, then top with thefudgy icing and Rice Krispie clusters.

ing: 1 cup cream or organic full cream milk
1 1/4 cups Whipping cream, whipped to firm peaks
1 Vanilla pod, split and seeds reserved
75 g good quality dark chocolate, roughly chopped
st: Whisk the milk, cream and cocoa in a saucepan over a medium heat.
Using an electric whisk, beat the egg yolks, vanilla seeds and sugar until thick and creamy. Whisk in the hot milk mixture and return to the saucepan.
Add the chocolate, whisk until melted, then simmer over a low heat until thick.
Transfer the ice-cream mixture into a bowl placed over iced water and whisk until cool. Once cooled, transfer to an ice-cream machine and churn according to manufacturerâs instructions.

ing: 200 g leeks, washed and roughly chopped
2 sweetcorn on the cob, sliced off the cob
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C. Grease or line a 20 x 6 cm pie dish or cast-iron frying pan with greaseproof paper.
Heat a nonstick frying pan over a medium heat and cook the sausages until just golden. Do not overcook. Remove from the pan and cut each sausage into four pieces.
Heat the butter and olive oil in the same pan and gently cook the leeks and garlic for 1 minute.

Place the pastry on a lightly floured board. Cut it lengthways into 3 cm-wide strips, then cut each strip into three âlegsâ, 1 cm wide, leaving a small piece intact at the top. Plait each piece of pastry, then chill for 15 minutes.
Whisk together the eggs, cream and cheese. Add the leeks and corn and season. Pour into the pie dish and stud with the sausages.

Gently place the pastry plaits around the edges and pinch the ends together to seal. Brush with milk. Bake for 30 minutes or until the mixture has set. Allow to stand for 5 minutes, then remove from the pan.

ing: 1/2 preserved lemon, flesh and pith removed and zest rinsed and finely sliced
1/2 preserved lemon, rinsed and finely chopped
6 fillets of sustainable white fish (cut into 150g portions)
st: Combine all the ingredients for the chermoula and pulse to a coarse paste in a food processor.
Preheat the oven to 180Â°C and grease a large baking tray.
Place the fish fillets in a single layer on the tray and spread with a tablespoon of the chermoula.
Bake in the oven for about 10 minutes. The fish should just start to flake.

ing: 4 outside lettuce leaves to steam on (or thick baking paper or foil)
4 firm, white, sustainable fish fillets cut into 150g portions
st: Warm a pan to medium heat, add the oils, then the red pepper, garlic and ginger and sautÃ© for 2-3 minutes. It must become soft, but not brown.
Remove from the heat and add the lemon juice, soy, sesame and spring onion and mix well.
Spread the mixture onto the fish fillets and place on lettuce leaves in a bamboo steamer.
Place the steamer tightly on top of a boiling pot and steam the rolled fish fillets for 8- 10 minutes until just cooked. (For added flavour, steam over fish stock.)
Steam just before serving and garnish with the more fresh spring onion.
Serve with steamed brown rice or an Asian salad.
Cut the sweet potatoes into skinny 2cm thick wedges, about 5cm long.
Place potatoes wedges in a pot with a good pinch of salt and bring to the boil. Allow to boil for 8 minutes.  Remove the sweet potatoes from the pot and allow them to steam dry.
Place in a large roasting tray in a single layer and add the olive oil and seasoning.
Place in a preheated oven at 200Â°C for about 30 minutes and bake until golden and crispy.
Place on a platter and serve with the guacamole.

ing: 1 tbsp almond butter or peanut butter with no added salt or sugar
200 g strawberries (replace with mango, other berries, pineapple for variation)
st: Place yoghurt, milk, oats and nut butter in a food processer and blend until smooth - about 5 minutes.
Add the fruits and honey and continue blending for an additional 3 minutes.
Pour into chilled glasses and serve chilled.
To produce chilled smoothies easily, use frozen berries or freeze the banana the night before.

ing: 6 tsp nut butter (homemade or with no sugar/salt )
8 tbsp homemade granola / Slimmer's Choice Swiss muesli
st: Core the apples using an apple corer, then slice each apple into thick slices â about 3 or 4 per apple.
Spread the nut butter on the apple and sprinkle with the homemade granola.
Place the dried chickpeas in a bowl and cover with 1.5L of cold water. Soak dried chickpeas in the water over night.
In the morning drain the chickpeas and place in a pot on the stove with plenty of water. Bring to the boil and then simmer until the chickpeas are al dente, then drain.
Allow chickpeas to cool before transferring to the food processer.
(If using the tinned chickpeas thendrain and rinse well then place in food processor)

While the chickpeas are boiling cut the broccoli into small florets, wash them then place on a roasting tray.  Drizzle with the canola oil and season lightly with salt and pepper.  Place in the oven and roast for about 20 minutes.  Remove from the oven and allow to cool.
Add the broccoli, garlic, parsley, onion, spices and water to the chickpeas in the food processer.
Blend until the mixture is smooth. Stop the machine at times to scrape down the sides to allow for all the ingredients to blend thoroughly.
Remove the falafel mixture from the food processor and roll into 30g balls, then press each ball down to form a patty.
When all the falafel balls are rolled and shaped, dip each one into beaten egg then roll in the sesame seeds until evenly coated. Repeat until all are coated.
Place in the oven and bake at 180ËC until the sesame seeds are a golden colour.
Remove from the oven and serve with harissa and low fat yoghurt.

ing: 2 tins cannellini beans, drained and rinsed
4 large fresh tomatoes, skinned, seeded and chopped into cubes.
120 g leeks, halved and thinly sliced
st: Warm a large pot and add the oil. When the oil is hot add the onions and sautÃ© for 5 minutes. Turn down the heat slightly and add the carrots, leeks and fennel and cook for a further 5 minutes on a low heat.
Add tomato puree, sugar and vegetable stock.  Bring to the boil then turn down the heat and allow liquid to simmer for half an hour.

Add the beans, chopped tomato, spinach and chives and cook for another 20 minutes. If the soup seems too thin, remove about one cup of soup and puree finely in a food processor, then return it to the pot and cook for another five minutes.
Check the seasoning and serve.
Garnish with more fresh chives.

ing: 250 ml homemade or free-range chicken stock
1/2 preserved lemon, pith and pulp removed, rinsed and finely chopped.
6 chicken thighs, skin removed with bone in
st: Combine the garlic, paprika, cumin, pepper, 15ml olive oil, and the chicken and marinate for at least one hour, but ideally overnight.
Heat the remaining oil in a casserole and brown the chicken on all sides. Then remove and set aside.
Finely chop the onion and sautÃ© until golden then add the saffron and olives. Cook for two minutes.
Return the chicken to the casserole and add the lemon juice, preserved lemon or lemon slices, honey and cup of chicken stock.
Bring to boil then cover with a lid and simmer for approximately 15 minutes, basting regularly. After 15 minutes remove lid and if necessary reduce the liquid to a thick sauce.
Garnish with coriander and serve with whole-wheat couscous.
Pre-heat the oven to 200ËC.
Place the onion, garlic, ginger, ground cinnamon, ground cumin, salt and pepper in food processer and blend until it resembles a chunky paste.
Place the beef mince in a bowl and add the onion spice paste.
Add the chopped herbs to the mixture and check the seasoning.
Shape the mince into 30g balls, and shape each into an oval and set aside.
Soak the skewers in cold water for at least 15 minutes before inserting into the oval beef koftas.
Place the yoghurt in a bowl and add the honey and mix well.
Place saffron in a cup and add 1tbsp boiling water, leave to steep before adding to the yogurt. Mix well and keep chilled until ready to serve.
Place the koftas on a baking tray greased with the oil and bake until golden, turning the meatballs around after about 7 minutes. You can also cook them under the grill if you need more colour.
Serve with the saffron yoghurt and garnish with coriander leaves.
Remove most of the fat layer from the sirloin as well as the sinew under the fat.
Place the sirloin in a tray and pat dry.
Combine all the dry ingredients in a bowl.
Crush the garlic and onion with olive oil in a mortar and add to the dry ingredients.
Rub the mixture into sirloin and leave to marinate for up to 1 hour.
Pre-heat the oven to 200Â°C.
Remove sirloin from the tray and brush off excess marinade.
Heat a cast iron grill pan and brown the sirloin on all sides.
Place sirloin in the oven and cook for 15- 20 minutes until 58-60Â°C internal temperature.  Remove from the oven and allow to rest.
Carve and serve.
Slice the baby marrows lengthwise into 3mm strips and season with the salt. Set aside for about 30 minutes.
In the meantime, combine the crushed garlic and olive oil and set aside.
Crumble the feta and slice the sundried tomatoes into strips.
After 30 minutes, wipe the moisture off the baby marrows and place them on a baking tray.
Brush with the olive oil and garlic on both sides.
Pre-heat the oven grill and cook the baby marrows about a three minutes a side under the grill.
Allow to cool, then place three basil leaves with a piece of sundried tomato onto each baby marrow slice, sprinkle the feta over as well as some black pepper and roll them up.
Serve at room temperature.
Pre-heat oven to 160ËC.
Toast ground almonds in the oven until golden.  Remove from the oven and allow to cool.
Blend almonds and dates in a food processer until the mixture comes together.
Line a 20cm tart tine with the ground almond mixture and place in the refrigerator until needed.
Roast pecan nuts and macadamia nuts in the oven until they are releasing aroma.
Heat the milk on the stove until it comes to the boil.  Pour over the chocolate and whisk until all the chocolate has melted.
Allow to cool slightly before adding the eggs which have been whisked slightly.
Pour chocolate mixture into tart shell and decorate with the toasted nuts on top.  Make a creative pattern with the nuts.
Place tart in the oven and bake for 35 minutes or until set.   Remove from the oven.
Place honey and water in a tea cup and melt in the microwave.  Brush the top of the chocolate tart with the honey glaze.
Garnish with mint and serve.
Peel the bananas and cut each bananas into 3-4cm sized cylinders.
Place bananas on a tray and place in the freezer for at least 30 minutes.
Chop the peanuts very fine on a chopping board and set aside.
Place the chocolate in a plastic bowl and melt in the microwave.  Stop the microwave after every 30 seconds to stir the chocolate to make sure it does not seize.

Dip the bananas into the melted chocolate then place on the baking tray sprinkle the top of the banana with the chopped peanuts.  When all the bananas have been dipped return to the freezer until ready to serve.
Heat the oil and add the whole crushed garlic, onion, carrot and celery and sautÃ© gently until translucent. Add the tomato concentrate and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomato, bay, salt and sugar and simmer for about 1 hour.
Remove the bay leaf and puree with a hand blender, but not too smooth.
Tear basil leaves into the sauce.
Check seasoning.
Cool down and freeze once cold in 500ml portions.

ing: 1/2 cucumber, seeded and chopped in small cubes
1  big handful Italian parsley, finely chopped
3 plum tomatoes, seeds removed and cut in small cubes
st: Marinate the chicken breasts in a bowl with canola oil, black pepper and lemon zest for half an hour.
In another bowl whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, garlic and honey together and set aside.
Place bulgur wheat in a large bowl, season lightly and top with the boiling water. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and allow it to stand for about 20 minutes.
Flake the bulgur wheat with a fork then add the dressing and combine well. Add the chopped tomato and cucumber, parsley, spring onions and mint.
Place in the fridge to chill.
Season and then grill the chicken breast on a griddle pan until cooked and allow to cool before slicing into blocks.
Toss the chicken through the bulgur wheat salad and check the seasoning. Garnish with mint and serve.
Cut the tuna in to 2cm cubes.
Place the coriander seeds into a dry pan on the stove and toast the seeds until there natural aroma is released.
In a spice blender or mortar and pestle, crush the coriander seeds coarsely.
Place all remaining ingredients into a food processer and blend until you have a chunky paste.
Pour marinade over tuna cubes and leave for at least 20 minutes, then remove from the marinade and skewer onto bamboo cocktail skewers.
Warm up a grill pan and sear the tuna on all sides until they are golden brown. Brush with a bit of marinade at it cooks. Discard the rest of the marinade.
Remove from the heat and serve immediately, garnish with lime wedges and coriander leaves.
Preheat the oven to 180ËC.
Scrub the potatoes well, but retain the skin.

Place the potatoes on a chopping board and with a sharp knife slice two thirds into the potato, the slices should be 2mm apart.  Slice from the one side of the potato right up to the other end.  Repeat this step with the remaining potatoes.
Place the potatoes in a large bowl.  Add the oil, salt, paprika, lemon juice and half the zest.  Toss the potatoes well in the spice mixture then place on a roasting tray.
Bake for 1 hour.
Place parmesan cheese and remaining zest of 1 lemon in a bowl and mix.
Remove the potatoes from the oven and sprinkle the parmesan and lemon zest over.
Return to the oven and bake for a further 20 minutes, remove from the oven and serve. With fish or meat main course and salads.
Cut the yellowtail into more or less 2cm cubes and set aside.
Soak the skewers in cold water for 15 minutes before skewering the yellowtail.  In a bowl mix the curry powder, orange zest, orange juice, ginger, black pepper, oil and curry leaves and mix well.
Pour marinade over the yellowtail and leave for an hour to infuse.
Pre-heat oven to 180ËC.
Skewer three cubes of yellowtail onto each skewer.
Heat a griddle pan and cook the skewers briefly, making sure to get good griddle lines on all sides.
Remove skewers from the pan and baste with the marinade and place on a tray in the oven. Continue to cook for 5-7 minutes.
Remove from the oven and serve, garnish with orange zest and coriander leaves.

ing: 1 bouquet garnish (parsley, thyme, bay leaf, black pepper)
st: Cut the fat off the bones and roast the bones in a hot oven until dark in colour.
Cut the vegetables into large blocks and brown in a pot with 15ml vegetable oil
Add the bones to the pot and continue cooking.
Then deglaze the sediment that formed at the bottom of the pot with a bit of water or with the wine.
Add the tomato paste and cook for 5 minutes, then deglaze again with water or wine. Make sure the tomato paste does not burn or it will become very bitter.
Add the bouquet garni to the pot.
Top up with cold water and bring to the boil.
Reduce the heat to a simmer and skim continuously.
Simmer for at least 6 hours. Larger quantities can be cooked up to 12 hours.
Strain through a muslin cloth or fine sieve and cool down.
Stock can be reduced and frozen in ice trays or small bags for later use in cooking.

t: Corn, red pepper & red onion salsa
st: Steam the cob for 5 minutes and slice the kernels off the cob.
Cut the peppers into squares the size of the corn.
Combine the corn, peppers and red onion.
Add the olive oil, coriander and seasoning.
Mix well and refrigerate.
Serve as an accompaniment to the Cajun sirloin.

ing: 400 g tuna steak, frozen and thinly sliced
sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
st: Heat the oil in a pan and fry the pancetta until golden. Add the garlic and ciabatta and fry until crispy and golden.

ing: sea salt and white pepper, to taste
500 g Conchiglie Pasta, cooked al dente
2 x 100 g packets Woolworths sliced smoked Italian pancetta, roughly chopped
st: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C. Fry the pancetta over a medium to high heat, or until golden and crisp. Add the cream and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer until reduced by half. Season to taste.
Remove from the heat and whisk in the egg.

Place the cooked pasta into a baking dish with the chicory, kale and Gorgonzola. Pour over the sauce and bake for 10â15 minutes, or until golden and bubbling. Sprinkle over the Parmesan before serving.

ing: 2 x 400 g cans cannellini beans, drained
2 x 35 g packets Woolworths Italian hunter-style salami
3 leeks, washed and chopped into 4 equal pieces
2 stalks celery, chopped into 5 equal pieces
3 carrots, peeled and chopped into chunks
st: Place everything except the salami into a medium-sized saucepan and cover with water. Bring to the boil, then reduce the heat to a simmer. Simmer for 1 hour, skimming the surface from time to time. Top up with more water if necessary. Remove the chicken and break into pieces. Add the salami to the broth 5 minutes before serving.
To make the cannellini mash, place all the ingredients into a blender and blend until smooth and thick, adding a little hot water to loosen if necessary. Season with salt.
To make the gremolata, mix all the ingredients and toss until evenly coated.
To serve, place a spoonful of mash into warmed bowls. Place the chicken and vegetables around the mash and ladle in the hot broth. Serve with the gremolata.
Trim the baby marrows, slice into 3 mm long strips and remove the seeds.
Mix the flour and eggs. Dip the baby marrows into the batter and fry in the hot oil for 5 minutes, or until golden. Drain on kitchen paper and season.

ing: maldon salt and pepper, to taste
150 g Woolworths fresh fior di latte mozzarella, torn
st: Sign in/Register

ing: sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C. Heat the butter and the olive oil in a large castiron pan. Layer the fennel, garlic and lemon in the pan, then cover tightly with foil and a lid. Cook over a gentle heat for 20 minutes, then place in the oven and cook for 30 minutes.
Remove the foil and lid. The fennel should have a charred base and a soft, caramelised texture.
Soak the gelatine leaves in the milk for 5 minutes to soften.
Heat the cream and sugar in a saucepan over a medium heat, whisking to dissolve the sugar. Bring the cream to a simmer, then remove from the heat.

Pour the gelatine-and-milk mixture into the warm cream and whisk. Add the chocolate and cocoa and continue whisking until smooth. Divide the mixture equally between 4 greased dariole moulds and chill for 2 hours or until set.
To make the poached prunes, heat the vino cotto in a pan over a medium heat. Add the prunes and grapes and cook for 5â10 minutes, or until soft.
To remove the panna cotta from the moulds, dip into a bowl of hot water for 5 seconds. Gently loosen the edges using a knife and turn out onto serving plates.
Serve with the poached prunes and an espresso.

ing: 1 1/2 ground cinnamon, plus extra, for dusting
1 vanilla pod, split and seeds scraped
500 g plain full fat cream cheese, softened
st: Preheat oven to 150Â°C.
Place the ginger cookies and ground almonds in a food processor and process until coarsely chopped.
Add the butter and process to combine.
Using the back of a spoon, press the mixture into the bases and sides of 8 x 8cm-round lightly greased, deep-sided and loose-bottomed tart tins. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
To make the filling, place the cream cheese and sour cream in an electric mixer and beat for 3â4 minutes or until smooth.
Add the sugar, vanilla seeds, mixed spice, cinnamon and ginger and beat for 3â4 minutes or until the sugar is dissolved.
Gradually add the eggs, beating well after each addition until well combined.
Divide the mixture between the tart tins, place on a baking tray and bake for 15â20 minutes or until firm to the touch.
Refrigerate for 6 hours or overnight until the crusts have set.
Dust with the extra cinnamon to serve.

ing: Sriracha Hot Chilli Sauce, to serve
1/2 cup sour cream, plus extra to serve
sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
225 g chorizo, case removed and chopped
st: Place the chorizo in a small food processor and process until finely chopped.

Heat the oil in a large non-stick frying pan over a high heat. Add the chicken, chorizo, garlic, chilli, salt and pepper and cook, breaking up any lumps with a wooden spoon, for 12â15 minutes or until browned and cooked through.
Divide the chicken mixture between the tortillas.
Top with the avocado, tomatoes, sour cream and coriander.
Serve with the chilli sauce, lime and extra sour cream.

t: Apple and ginger sour cream cake
ing: 300 (approximately 2 medium)  g Granny Smith apples, peeled, cored and thinly sliced
1 tbsp honey, plus extra to serve
120 g unsalted butter, softened plus 20g, melted
st: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C.
Place the 120g softened butter, sugar, vanilla and lemon rind in an electric mixer and beat for 8â10 minutes or until pale and creamy.
Scrape down the sides of the bowl, add the egg and beat well to combine.
Add the flour, ginger and sour cream and beat on low until just combined.
Spoon the mixture into a lightly greased 20cm square tin lined with non-stick baking paper and spread evenly.
Place the apple, 20g melted butter and honey in a bowl and toss to combine. Arrange the apple on top of the cake in 3 neat, straight rows of overlapping slices.
Cook for 55â60 minutes or until golden and cooked through.
Allow to cool in the tin for 10 minutes before drizzling with extra honey. Slice while warm with extra sour cream to serve.

ing: salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 loaf rusticata bread, cut into 12 thin slices
freshly ground black pepper, to serve
2 tbsp sour cream, plus extra to serve
1 leek, white part only, thinly sliced
st: Heat the butter and oil in a large saucepan over a medium heat.
Add the onion, leek and garlic and stir occasionally until tender, about 7 - 10 minutes.
Add the cauliflower, stir to coat in butter, add the stock and simmer until very tender for 40 - 45 minutes.
Add the milk; bring to a simmer, then purÃ©e in a blender until very smooth.
Stir in the Gruberg or GruyÃ¨re cheese, sourcream and mustard, season to taste and keep warm.
For the garlic toast, preheat the grill to high. Process the butter, Parmesan, garlic and herbs in a food processor until smooth and season to taste.

Place the bread slices on a baking tray, drizzle with oil, season to taste and grill, turning once, until golden. Spread with garlic butter, drizzle over good olive oil and add a dollop of sour cream to serve with the soup and toasts.

ing: salt and freshly ground black pepper
st: Heat a grill pan over a high heat. Cook the corn, turning occasionally, for 10 minutes or until charred. Set aside.

Thread the 3 chicken thighs onto skewers. Brush the chicken with half the oil and sprinkle with salt and pepper. Cook the chicken in batches for 5 minutes each side or until charred and cooked through.
While the chicken is cooking, place the chilli, spring onion, coriander, lime juice, salt, pepper and remaining oil in a food processor and process until finely chopped.
Cut the sweet corn kernels from the cobs, place in a large bowl with the chilli mixture and toss to combine.
Serve the chicken with the corn salsa, sour cream and naan breads.

ing: 1/4 cup crispy onion sprinkles, to serve
1 can chickpeas, rinsed and patted dry
1 x 5 cm piece ginger, peeled and finely grated
salt and freshly ground black pepper
st: For the pickled chillies, combine the chillies, vinegar, sugar, salt and water in a bowl. Mix until the sugar dissolves, then set aside.
Preheat the oven to 200 Â°C.

For the cauliflower, toss the florets with the olive oil and salt on a rimmed baking sheet. Roast for about 30 â 35 minutes, tossing occasionally, until the cauliflower is tender and browned. Transfer to paper towels to drain and set aside.
For the curry, heat the oil in a large skillet over a medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 5 â 7 minutes, stirring often.
Add the ginger, garlic and lemongrass and cook for about 1 minute, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
Add the tomato paste and harissa paste and cook for about 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until slightly darkened in colour.
Whisk in the coconut milk, bring the sauce to a boil and cook for 5 â 7 minutes, whisking occasionally, until the sauce becomes thick and creamy.
Add the chickpeas and 1/4 cup of water and cook, stirring occasionally, until the mixture returns to a boil. Remove from the heat, stir in the chopped coriander and season.
Serve the curry with the jasmine rice, topped with the drained pickled chillies, roasted cauliflower, crispy onion sprinkles and microherbs with poppadums on the side.
Preheat oven to 150Â°C.
Place the egg whites in the bowl of an electric mixer and whisk on high speed until stiff peaks form.
Add the sugar, 1 tablespoon at a time, whisking for 30 seconds before adding more. Once all the sugar has been added whisk for a further 6 minutes or until stiff and glossy.
Scrape down the side of the bowl, add the vinegar and whisk for a further 2 minutes or until glossy and combined.
Draw a 26cm circle on a sheet of non-stick baking paper and place on a lightly greased baking tray.
Spoon 1 cup of the meringue into the centre of the circle, leaving a 5cm border. Arrange heaped spoonfulâs of meringue around the circle to create a ring.
Reduce the heat to 120Â°C and bake for 1 hour 30 minutes or until crisp. Turn the oven off and allow the Pavlova to cool for 1 hour 30 minutes. Remove from the oven and cool.

To make the candied pecans, heat a small saucepan over a medium heat. Add the pecans, sugars, vanilla and Â¼ cup water and cook, stirring occasionally, for 6â7 minutes or until golden and caramelised. Transfer immediately to a tray lined with non-stick baking paper and spread to cool completely. Roughly chop and set aside.
Place the cream, crÃ¨me fraÃ®che and Â¼ cup of the icing sugar in a large bowl and whisk until stiff peaks form. Fold through 1 teaspoon of the cinnamon until just combined.
Transfer the Pavlova to a plate, top with the cream and sprinkle with the pecans.
Mix to combine the remaining icing sugar and cinnamon and dust over the Pavlova to serve. Decorate with shards of pecan praline or brittle if you like.

ing: salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 Hot bird's eye chilli, seeds removed and finely chopped
salt and freshly ground black pepper
st: Combine all the salsa ingredients, season and mix well to combine.
Combine all the lamb pattie ingredients in a bowl, season and mix to combine.
Handling the meat as lightly as possible to avoid compressing it too much, shape it into 4 patties.
Heat a large frying pan over a medium heat for 2 â 3 minutes, then add the patties and cook, undisturbed, for 3 minutes for medium. Turn over to cook the other side for another 3 minutes.
Serve the lamb patties with the fresh mango salsa.

ing: salt and freshly ground black pepper
1/2 red onion, thinly sliced into slivers
1/2 red onion, thinly sliced into slivers
st: Place the baby potatoes and salt in a large pot with enough water to cover. Bring to a boil over a high heat, then reduce to a gentle boil.
Cook the potatoes for about 15 â 20 minutes until they are tender when pierced with a knife.
Drain in a colander and allow to cool for a few minutes.
Cut the potatoes in half and drizzle with the vinegar. Set aside to cool.
Place the eggs in a small pan with enough water to cover and place over a medium-high heat. When the water comes to a boil, turn off the heat, cover and allow to stand for 12 minutes.
Drain and place the eggs in a bowl with enough cold water to cover.
When cold, peel the hard-boiled eggs and cut into quarters lengthwise.
Place the mayonnaise and curry powder in a large bowl and whisk to combine.
Add the potatoes, eggs, onion and coriander, season and stir to combine. Chill until ready to serve.
Preheat the oven to 180 Â°C and grease a baking sheet.
Place the cashew nuts on another baking sheet and roast until lightly golden.
In a medium saucepan, dissolve the sugar, glucose and 1/4 cup of water over a low heat.
Once all the sugar has dissolved, bring the mixture to a boil, swirling occasionally, until just starting to change colour.
Add the salt, curry powder and cashews, and stir making sure the cashews are completely coated and the spices are evenly combined.
Continue to cook, swirling constantly, until the caramel is a deep golden brown and the cashews are toasted.
Remove from the heat and carefully stir in the butter and bicarbonate of soda.
Immediately pour the mixture onto the greased baking sheet, using a spatula to spread it as thinly as possible.
Allow to cool, then break the brittle into uneven pieces.

ing: 12 mange tout, stemmed, tough strings removed and thinly sliced
1/2 red pepper, medium size, stemmed, seeded and julienned
100 g smoked ham, cut into thin slices
2 eggs, beaten with two pinches of salt
200 g Frozen ready to cook peeled prawns, defrosted
st: Combine the prawns in a bowl with 1 teaspoon of canola oil and 1 teaspoon of fish sauce, mix well and place in the fridge.

Place the noodles in a large bowl and cover with boiling water. Allow to stand for 5 minutes, then drain in a colander and rinse with cold running water. Drain until dry, then cut the noodles in half with a pair of scissors.
Mix the garlic in a small bowl with the soya sauce, white pepper, sugar and the remaining fish sauce. Mix well and set aside.

Heat 1 teaspoon of canola oil in a wok over a high heat until smoking. Add the eggs and cook undisturbed for 10 seconds, then gently move the eggs with a spatula until they start to firm up. Break the eggs into small pieces, and set aside in a large bowl.
Wipe the wok clean and return it to a high heat. Add 2 teaspoons of oil, heat until smoking, then add the prawns and stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Add the smoked ham and onion and stir-fry for another 30 seconds.
Add the red pepper, mange tout and curry powder, and stir-fry for another 30 seconds, then add the carrots.
Empty the wokâs contents into the bowl with the egg and wipe the wok clean.

Heat the 2 tablespoons of canola oil over a high heat until smoking. Add the noodles and stir-fry for 30 seconds, then add the garlic soya sauce mixture and the remaining curry powder, and stir until the powder is evenly distributed.
Return the egg, prawns, smoked ham and vegetables to the wok and stir-fry for about 30 seconds until everything is combined.
Remove from the heat, add the spring onions and drizzle with sesame oil.
Mix well and transfer to a large, warmed bowl to serve.

ing: salted roasted peanuts, chopped, for sprinkling
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: Quarter the butternut lengthways.
Steam until tender, about 15â20 minutes. Season lightly.
Serve with the Thai peanut sauce and coriander rice. Sprinkle with chopped peanuts.

t: Cabbage rolls with pink pad Thai
st: Remove 6 outer leaves from a medium-sized cabbage. Blanch in boiling water then wrap in a damp cloth. Shred the remaining cabbage.
In a Teflon-coated frying pan, stir-fry the peeled prawns and chicken mince in a little olive oil.
Add the garlic, chilli and a few drops of sesame oil, then fry for another 4 minutes.
Stir through the shredded cabbage then remove from the heat and allow to cool.
Season to taste then stir through the mint.
Place the cabbage leaves on a flat surface. Spoon a generous helping of the prawn-chicken mixture onto each leaf, then roll up tightly with the sides folded in.
Tightly pack the rolls into a bamboo steamer then steam for 30 minutes.
Heat the oil in a medium-sized wok and add the onions, mushrooms and garlic. Toss for 1 to 2 minutes, or until caramelised. Remove from the wok and set aside.
Cut the ox liver into 2 cm pieces and dust with the salt and cornflour. Dust off any excess cornflour.
Stir-fry the liver in the wok until crisp on the surface but undercooked in the middle, about 30 seconds. Remove from the wok and set aside.
Deglaze the pan with the wine and reduce to a glaze. Add the vinegar and oyster sauce and simmer slowly until slightly thickened.
Add the onions and liver and stir-fry for 2 minutes, or until the liver is just cooked.
Serve garnished with the spring onions and sesame seeds.

ing: 4 spring onions (green parts), chopped, for sprinkling
4 spring onions (white parts only), finely chopped
st: Slice the pork into strips. Mix the pork with the salt, then mix in the vinegar, soya sauce and 1 T cornflour. Add the egg white and mix by hand until well coated. Allow to stand at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Drop the pork into a saucepan of boiling water for barely a minute. Drain.
Fry in batches in medium-hot oil until nicely coloured. Set aside.

In a clean pan, heat 2 T oil. Stir in the spring onion. Cook, stirring, for barely a minute. Stir in the ginger, garlic and chilli. Pour in the stock and naartjie juice and bring to a simmer. Stir in the honey and hoisin sauce, then add the fried pork and heat through. Mix the remaining cornflour with 1 T water and stir in until the sauce thickens. Serve with the soya-sesame noodles.

To make the soya-sesame noodles, bring a large saucepan of water to the boil. Add the noodles and vegetables and simmer for 4â5 minutes, or until the noodles are tender. Drain and mix with the soya sauce and sesame oil.

ing: 4 tbsp unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
st: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C.
Peel the skin off the top quarter of each apple and using a melon baller, scoop out the core, leaving the bottom intact.
Stand the apples upright in a 33 x 23 x 5 cm baking pan.
Mix the sugar and spices in a bowl. Reserve 2 tablespoons of the mixture.

Fill the apple cavities with the remaining sugar mixture. Spoon Â½ a tablespoon of maple syrup into each cavity and scatter 3 tablespoons of butter over the apples. This can be done up to 4 hours before baking and kept covered in the fridge until needed.
Pour Â½ cup of water into the pan with the apples and bake for 35 minutes.
Add the reserved 2 tablespoons of sugar mixture, 2 tablespoons of maple syrup, 1 tablespoon of butter and Â½ cup of water to the pan.
Bake for another 25 minutes or until the apples are tender when pierced with a skewer.
Transfer the apples to 8 individual serving bowls.
Place the baking pan on the stove and boil over a medium-high heat for about 2 minutes until the mixture becomes syrupy.
Spoon the sauce over the apples and serve with double cream.

t: Banana coffee cashew and cocoa smoothie
ing: a pinch cardamom pods, cracked open
1/4 cup raw cashews, preferably soaked overnight
st: Using the smoothie or ice crush setting on a blender, purÃ©e all the ingredients together with Â½ cup of ice until smooth.
Serve immediately.

ing: freshly ground black pepper, to taste
1 butternut, peeled and cut into 12 x 3 mm round slices through the neck of the butternut
1 egg, beaten with 1 teaspoon of water
1 x 250 g sheet all butter puff pastry, defrosted
st: Preheat the oven to 190Â°C.
Line a large, rimmed baking sheet with baking paper.
Gently lay the sheet of puff pastry on the baking sheet and brush with the egg wash.

Arrange the butternut rounds over the pastry, overlapping as needed and leaving a 1.5 cm border. Place another sheet of baking paper over the butternut and set another large rimmed baking sheet over the baking paper to weigh down the pastry, and cook the butternut slices.
Bake for about 10 minutes, until the bottom of the pastry begins to brown and the top begins to puff.
Remove the top baking sheet and discard the top sheet of baking paper. Brush the butternut slices with 1 tablespoon of olive oil and season with salt.
Return the tart, uncovered, to the oven and bake for a further 25-30 minutes until the pastry is a deep golden brown and cooked through.
Meanwhile, combine the honey, chilli and 2 tablespoons of water in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil over a medium heat and boil for about 6 minutes, until slightly thickened and syrupy.
Line a plate with paper towel.
Heat the remaining olive oil in a small pan until just beginning to smoke. Add the fresh sage leaves and fry for about 30 seconds until crisp. Transfer to the paper towel to drain.
To serve, slice the butternut tart, sprinkle with the shaved Parmesan, drizzle with the chilli-infused honey and garnish with the fried sage leaves and freshly ground black pepper.

ing: salt and freshly ground black pepper
9 tbsp olive oil, plus extra for drizzling
900 g beetroot, scrubbed, tops and root ends trimmed
st: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C.
Place one quarter of the scrubbed beetroot on a large sheet of foil, drizzle with 2 tablespoons of olive and seal the foil tightly on all sides to make a parcel. Repeat with the remaining beetroot.
Cook in a preheated oven for 1 hour or until the beetroot is tender when pierced with a knife.
Cool and remove the skins.
Place the beetroot into a food processor. Add the lemon juice, sesame seeds, 1 tablespoon of olive oil and garlic, and process until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
Drizzle the baba ghanoush with extra olive oil and top with sumac or zaâatar or toasted sesame seeds as desired.
Serve with warm pita bread.

ing: 60 g butter, plus extra for greasing
st: Heat the oven to 180 Â°C.
Grease and line the base and sides of a 20 cm round cake tin with baking paper.
Mix the flour, baking powder and cinnamon together in a large bowl.
Melt the honey, sugar and butter together in a small saucepan over a low heat.
In a separate bowl, mash the bananas with a fork then mix in the beaten eggs.
Make a well in the centre of the flour and pour in the melted butter and sugar mixture, and beat together.
Add the banana and egg mixture and beat again, then fold in the raisins.
Transfer the mixture to the prepared cake tin and level the surface.
Scatter with the flaked almonds and bake for 50 minutes â 1 hour, or until a skewer inserted comes out clean. Cover the cake with foil after about 40 minutes if the surface is browning too quickly.
Remove from the oven and leave to cool in the tin.

t: Chinese beef with a black pepper sauce
ing: freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: Whisk together the soy sauce, honey, oyster sauce, chicken stock, 2 tablespoons of water and black pepper and set aside.
For the stir fry, heat the peanut oil in a wok or large heavy-based pan over a high heat until it is smoking.
Add the onion and garlic and cook, stirring frequently, for 1 minute or until the onion becomes translucent.
Add the beef and stir fry for 40 seconds to 1 minute until just cooked to your liking. Remove from the wok or pan and set aside.
Turn the heat down to medium-high and add the sauce ingredients to the wok or pan. They will start simmering very quickly. Cook for 1 minute or until they become syrupy.
Add the beef and onion mixture to the sauce, along with any juices and toss for 1 minute at most until just warmed through. Do not overcook.

ing: salt and freshly ground black pepper
st: To make the glaze, combine the apple juice, apricot jam, apricots, onion marmalade and mustard in a saucepan over a medium heat.
Bring to a boil, reduce the heat, and simmer for 15 minutes or until syrupy.
Preheat a grill pan.
Brush the kassler chops with oil and fry for 2 minutes on each side or until browned.
Pour over the glaze and cook for a further 2 â 3 minutes.
Season to taste and serve.

ing: 50 g pistachios, toasted and finely chopped
70 g sago soaked in water for 30 min, then drained
st: Heat butter in a large saucepan over medium heat, then add in 80g of the vermicelli, cardamom and cinnamon stick. Cook until golden brown whist continuously stirring.
Add in the milk and soaked sago and simmer for 35minutes, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking and burning.
Stir in the condensed milk, rose water and vanilla.
To make the topping, heat oil in a pan over medium high heat, once hot, fry 80 g vermicelli in batches until puffed, drain on paper towel.
Dust the puffed vermicelli in beetroot powder.
Serve the Boeber warm topped with puffed vermicelli and a sprinkle of nuts.

ing: sea salt and white pepper, to taste
st: Fry the pork sausages in a little oil over a medium heat until golden brown and cooked through. Set aside.
In the same frying pan, fry the onion in a little olive oil until soft. Add the chorizo, garlic, chilli and smoked paprika and fry for a further minute.
Add the tomato paste, crushed tomatoes and sugar. Cook over a medium heat for 10 minutes, or until thick, adding the olives and sausages after 5 minutes of cooking time. Season to taste.
Place in a serving dish and top with the poached eggs and a few dollops of yoghurt. Garnish with fresh coriander.

ing: 125 g country ham, cut into strips
30 g Parmesan, grated, plus extra for sprinkling
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: Stir-fry the mushrooms in the butter and oil over a high heat until just cooked and still fleshy. Remove from the pan and set aside.
Pour the cream into the pan, add the Parmesan and reduce until slightly thickened. Stir in the ham and mushrooms and heat through.
Microwave the baby marrow spaghetti according to package instructions. Gently mix with the sauce. Season to taste and sprinkle with Parmesan before serving.

ing: 1/3 cup crÃ¨me fraÃ®che, plus extra for serving
6 leaves sage, plus extra for serving
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C. Toss the celeriac in 2 T olive oil, season and roast for 20â25 minutes, turning occasionally, until brown and tender.

Meanwhile, soften the onion in the remaining olive oil for 5 minutes over a low heat until sweet but not brown. Increase the heat slightly and add the garlic and sage. Cook for 1 minute, add the stock and reduce for 10 minutes.
Blend the cauliflower until it reaches the consistency of rice. Fold into the onion mixture and cook for 5 minutes. Remove from the heat, stir in the crÃ¨me fraÃ®che and season.
Fry the extra sage leaves for 10 seconds, or until crisp. Serve the risotto with the celeriac, crÃ¨me fraÃ®che, fried sage and black pepper.

ing: sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
1 x 5 cm piece ginger, peeled and finely grated
st: Soften the onion in the oil for 5 minutes over a low heat, then add the ginger and garlic and cook for a further minute.
Increase the heat, add the mince and brown. Fold in the coconut milk and reduce slightly. Season and add the fish sauce. Serve with the sriracha sauce, coconut and noodles

ing: 1 x 400 g Italian tomatoes in juice
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: Preheat the oven to 190Â°C. Thinly slice the brinjals lengthways, then place in a bowl and mix by hand with the olive oil. Arrange in a single layer on baking sheets and bake for 15 minutes, or until tender. Season lightly.
Meanwhile, gently cook the onion in 2 T olive oil, then stir in the garlic. Increase the heat and add the mince. Keep stirring to break up the mince until the meat changes colour.

Crush the tomatoes using a potato masher, then add to the meat with the oregano and season to taste. Add the stock, cover and reduce the heat. Simmer, stirring now and again, for 40 minutes, or until very tender. Check the seasoning.
Remove the mince using a slotted spoon and set aside. Reduce the cooking liquid over a high heat until thick.

Increase the ovenâs temperature to 200Â°C. To assemble, place a layer of brinjal â about a third â in a 1-litre oiled baking dish. Cover with a layer of mince. Repeat with the remaining brinjals and mince. Spoon over the reduced cooking liquid and sprinkle with Parmesan. Bake for 20 minutes, or until browned.
Serve with rice or risoni and garnish with baby spinach.

ing: sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: Preheat the oven to 200Â°C. Mix the mince, cumin, parsley, oregano, balsamic glaze, seasoning, garlic, breadcrumbs, egg and mustard and shape into bite-sized meatballs.
Fry the meatballs in the olive oil over a medium heat for 5 minutes until browned, adding the cherry tomatoes for the last 2 minutes of cooking time.

Divide the mozzarella between the pizza bases and top with the panfried cherry tomatoes, meatballs and olives and bake for 10â15 minutes, or until golden and crisp. Serve hot with the basil, seasoning and a drizzle of olive oil.

ing: sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
100 g black olives, pitted and chopped
st: Heat the butter and olive oil in a large pan over a medium heat. Add the sage and fry for 20 seconds. Remove from the pan and do the same with the rosemary and bay leaves.
Add the onion to the herb-infused oil and sautÃ© until soft. Add the pork and beef mince and brown, then return the herbs to the pan.
Add the leeks, black olives and white wine and simmer. Once the wine has reduced by half, add the tomato passata, tomato paste, beef stock and sugar.
Combine all the ingredients and season to taste. Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 1Â½ hours, stirring occasionally.

To make the gnocchi, preheat the oven to 180Â°C. Roast the potatoes whole for 45 minutes, or until cooked through. Remove from the oven and cool. When cool enough to handle, peel and push the flesh through a potato ricer or grate using the fine side of a grater.
Place the potato into a bowl and add the egg yolks and salt. Sift in half the flour and knead to incorporate.

Slow sift in the remaining flour, a little at a time. Once all the flour has been added, the dough should be soft and spring back when pressed with your index finger. If the dough still feels wet, add 1 T flour at a time until it is no longer sticky.
Bring a saucepan of salted water to the boil. Divide the dough into 4 pieces, then roll into thin sausages and cut into 1.5 cm pieces.
Blanch the gnocchi in the salted, boiling water for 3â4 minutes, or until they rise to the surface. Remove using a slotted spoon and drizzle with olive oil to prevent them from sticking together.
To serve, spoon the Bolognese sauce over the gnocchi and top with grated Parmesan.

ing: 80 g Woolworths soft-eating Colourburst dried nectarines, chopped
st: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C and grease a 19 x 9 cm loaf tin.
Dissolve the yeast in the water. Grind the oats until fine in a blender or food processor, then add to the yeast mixture with the honey and coconut oil. Mix well.
Add the remaining ingredients and mix well. Pour into the greased loaf tin. Place in a warm place until doubled in size, about 45 minutes.
Top with whole oats and the flaked almonds and bake for 45 minutes.

ing: sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C. Mix the chicken mince with 3 spring onions, 1 grated green apple, the pecorino, seasoning, garlic, egg, mint and breadcrumbs.
Mould into golfball-sized balls. Roll in the sesame seeds, then arrange on a baking tray and drizzle with olive oil. Bake for 15â20 minutes, or until cooked through.
Cut the remaining apple into matchsticks and serve with the meatballs, remaining spring onion, lemon juice, cucumber, radish and pesto.

ing: rice, steamed with a few cracked Cardamom pods for serving
1 x 2 cm piece ginger, peeled and grated
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: Soften the onion in 2â3 T coconut oil. Stir in the brinjal, adding more oil if necessary, and cook over a fairly brisk heat for a few minutes. Remove from the pan and season lightly.

Reduce the heat to low. Add the remaining coconut oil, then stir in the curry powder, garlic and ginger. Add the beef mince and stir until coated with the spice mix. Season with salt and pour in the coconut cream.
Increase the heat slightly. Keep stirring until the mixture starts to bubble. Simmer gently, covered, for about 25 minutes, stirring now and again.

Return the brinjal and onion to the pan and cook for a further 15 minutes. Add the lime juice and sugar to taste. Add the carrots and check the seasoning. Sprinkle with chopped coriander and serve with the steamed rice, limes and lime pickle.

ing: salt and freshly ground black pepper
st: Preheat oven to 180Â°C. Coat the cauliflower florets in the olive oil and season with salt and freshly ground black pepper before placing on an oven tray and roasting for 30 minutes or until slightly charred but tender. Add the still hot cauliflower to a blender with the cream cheese until it resembles mashed potatoes.

For the filling: Heat the oil over a medium heat then add the mince to brown and caramelise. Add the garlic, carrots, celery, onion, red chilli and cook for 10 minutes to soften before adding the tomato paste, demi glace.  Stir before adding the water and seasoning then allow to reduce slightly.
Add the filling to a dish and top with the cauliflower mash. Place in the oven to cook for 30 minutes and serve.

ing: sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
100 g black olives, pitted and chopped
st: Heat the butter and olive oil in a large pan over a medium heat. Add the sage and fry for 20 seconds. Remove from the pan and do the same to the rosemary and the bay leaves.
Add the onion to the herb-infused oil and sautÃ© until soft. Add the pork and beef mince and brown, then return the herbs to the pan.

Add the leeks, black olives and white wine and simmer. Once the wine has reduced by half, add the tomato passata, tomato paste, beef stock and sugar. Combine all the ingredients and season to taste. Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 1Â½ hours, stirring occasionally.
Heat the oil over a high heat. Break the mince into small pieces and add to the pan to cook for 3 minutes or until crisp before turning over and crisping the other side.

Add the garlic, ginger, chilli and soy sauce along with the sweet chilli sauce. Stir-fry together for a minute before adding the coriander and rice and stirring into the mix. Once mixed through allow the rice to crisp slightly before adding the spring onions and tossing through.
Divide the mixture into 4 serving bowls before topping with a crispy fried egg and serving.

ing: 2 tsp fresh mint, finely chopped, plus extra to garnish
st: 1 Fry the mince until brown and slightly crispy.
Add the garlic, lime zest and juice, fish and hoisin sauces and fry for a further 5 minutes.
Remove from the heat and add the mint and coriander. Serve with the lettuce, onion, beans and garnish with mint.

t: Bobotie with brown rice and lentils
ing: salt and freshly ground black pepper
700 g free range lean beef mince
st: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C.
Gently cook the onion in the heated butter until meltingly soft and golden. Add the beef mince and pan fry for 5 minutes with the onion. Season to taste.
Tear the bread into bits and mash it with 65ml (Â¼ cup) of buttermilk and 1 beaten egg.
Mix the apricots, apple, raisins, sugar, curry powder and bay leaves then mix it with the mince and bread. Turn into a buttered baking dish (one large dish or individual dishes).
Beat the remaining 2 eggs with the rest of the buttermilk and the turmeric, and pour over the spiced meat mixture. Bake for 20 minutes or until the topping is set and golden.
Serve with brown and lentil rice and mango atchar.
Heat milk in a pot, then add the chocolate and stir until melted, remove from the heat, stir in the honey and yoghurt, then set aside.
Place butter, Demerara and syrup in a pan, and heat until butter melts and sugar dissolves.
Place banana, cut side down into the pan and leave to caramelize for 2 minutes before turning over.
Serve Bananas in bowls, topped with the ice cream and drizzled with the chocolate sauce, sprinkle with nuts to garnish.

ing: to serve raw flaked almonds, toasted
100 g dried apples and pears, chopped
st: In a bowl, combine the oats, bran, almonds, dried apples & pears, sunflower seeds, honey, yoghurt and milk then mix well and refrigerate overnight.
To serve, stir in the grated apple, then place into serving bowls.
Garnish with fresh fruit, toasted almonds and dried apricots.

ing: lime, cut into wedges, to serve
1 x 400 g tin organic Italian chopped tomatoes
700 g free range lean beef mince
st: For the chilli: Heat the coconut oil in a pan, add the garlic, onion, chili and spices, sautÃ© for 3 minutes, or until the onion is soft and golden. Add the beef mince and cook until browned; add the tomato paste and cook for another minute, then stir through the remaining ingredients.
Bring to the boil, reduce heat and simmer for 10-15 minutes.  Season.
For the aubergine: Heat coconut oil in a small saucepan. Fry aubergine slices until golden and crisp.  Toss together spices and seasoning and sprinkle over hot aubergine rounds.
To serve: Place the chili mince in 4 bowls, and serve with aubergine rounds, guacamole, tomato, fresh coriander and lettuce leaves.

ing: 4 Woolworths ultimate burger buns, lightly toasted
Woolworths smokey barbeque marinade, to glaze burgers
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: Divide the mince into 4 portions and flatten each patty slightly before adding a Babybel cheese to each patty. Carefully mold the mince around the cheese, sealing the cheese inside. Season the patty on the outside with salt and freshly ground black pepper and set aside while the oil is being heated over a medium heat.
Add the patties to the pan and cook for 4-5 minutes and ensure its well caramelized before turning over and covering with a lid, this allows the burger to steam as it browns.
Before removing the burger from the pan glaze the top with the BBQ marinade, turn over and glaze the other side. Remove from the heat. But keep the lid on the pan.
Add some of the slaw to the base of the burger buns. Add the glazed patties and finish with the top of the bun.

ing: 160 g Woolworths Plain Melba toast Slices
150 g Woolworths beef biltong snack sticks
freshly ground black pepper to taste
st: Combine all the ingredients for the spread in a blender and blend until a smooth spread is formed.
Serve with the Melba toast.
Cook the burger patties in a pan, then top with the cheese and allow to melt gently.
Slice the lettuce into thick slices (these will form the base of the burger),
Mix together the dressing ingredients, then drizzle generously onto the lettuce.
Top the dressed lettuce with the cheesy burger.
Mix together the salsa ingredients, then spoon on top of the burger patty.
Top with a fried egg and serve with an extra lime wedge.
For the chimichurri, place all the ingredients into a blender and blend until finely blended.
Heat a griddle pan until smoking hot. Season the steaks, then drizzle with olive oil.
Cook the steaks in the hot griddle then place onto a plate and drizzle with the chimichurri. Allow to stand and marinade for a few minutes while you assemble the rest of the sandwich.
Brush the bread with the oilive oil, then toast in the griddle pan on both sides.
Spread the toasted bread with some onion marmalade, then top with rocket and sliced tomatoes and finally the chimichurri steak.

ing: 50 ml sun-dried tomatoes in olive oil, finely chopped
st: Combine the mayonnaise and basil pesto in a small bowl.
Lay out 4 of the sourdough bread slices on a cutting board and spread liberally with the basil mayonnaise mixture.
Top with the tomato slices, cheese slices, sun-dried tomato and chopped spring onion.
Top with the remaining 4 slices of bread and drizzle with olive oil or the oil of the sun-dried tomatoes.
Place the 4 broodjies in a hinged braai grid and place them over low to medium-hot coals, oiled sides down.
Cook for a few minutes, drizzle with the olive oil or sun-dried tomato oil and turn the braai grid over.
Continue to braai over the coals, turning often, until the cheese has started melt and the broodjies are golden brown on both sides.

ing: 1/4 cup dill sprigs, chopped, to serve
sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, for seasoning
1 kg potatoes, scrubbed, halved and quartered
st: Place the quartered potatoes in a large saucepan of cold, salted water.
Place over a high heat, cover with a lid and bring to the boil. Remove the lid and cook for 8-10 minutes or until tender. Drain well and halve lengthways.
Preheat a chargrill pan or braai to a high heat.
Drizzle the potato with extra virgin olive oil, sprinkle with sea salt and freshly ground black pepper and cook, cut-side down, for 8-10 minutes or until lightly charred.
