Place the crÃ¨me fraiche, mustard, water, sea salt and freshly ground black pepper in a large bowl and mix to combine.
Place the potato on a serving plate, drizzle with the mustard dressing and top with dill to serve.

ing: salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
4 tbsp green olives, pitted and roughly chopped
1 lemon, zest peeled using vegetable peeler, and juiced
Woolworths heat and eat pita breads
salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
4 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, plus extra for brushing the koftas
st: To make the koftas: Heat the olive oil over a medium heat. Add the onions and garlic and season before stirring through and allow to sautÃ© until well caramelized without charring too much. If needed, reduce the heat to low to ensure the onions slowly brown.

Add the thyme, chilli flakes and sumac before allowing the flavours to marry for a few minutes until it becomes fragrant. Let the mixture cool before adding to the beef mince. Season with extra salt and pepper before mixing through and combining.
Shape about 2T of the mixture into a sausage shape or shape around a skewer. Brush lightly with extra olive oil. Heat a griddle pan or prepare a braai with medium heat coals.
Add the koftas and cook for about 3 minutes a side or until the meat is well caramelized.

To make the lemon and herb relish:Finely chop the lemon zest before adding to a mixing bowl before squeezing in the lemon juice. Combine the remaining ingredients and mix through before allowing it to sit for 15 minutes.
Serve the koftas with the lemon and herb relish as well as the pita breads, yoghurt and extra coriander to garnish.
Toast 1 tbsp cumin seeds and 1 tbsp coriander seeds in a dry pan.

In a food processor, combine the toasted cumin and coriander,  5 spring onions, 3 cm sized piece of ginger, 4 garlic cloves, 1 green chilli, 30 g coriander, 2 tbsp fish sauce, 4 tbsp sugar and apple juice. Blend until a fine paste.
Rub paste all over meat or fish before leaving to marinade overnight or for as long as possible.

ing: 2 x 250 g Woolworths streaky smoked bacon
salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: Heat the oil over a medium heat. Add the onion and garlic and season before cooking until well caramelized but not charred.
Add the rosemary and chilli flakes cook for an additional 5 minutes to marry the flavours. Remove from the heat and allow to cool.
Combine the cooled onion mixture with the mince and onion marmalade, set aside.

Lay a sheet of foil on a work surface, with the shiny side facing up. Arrange the streaks of bacon vertically, overlapping slightly over the sheet of foil. Add a layer of the spinach before seasoning lightly.
Add the mince filling at the bottom end of the bacon, keeping it as close to a sausage shape as possible.
Carefully begin rolling the bacon over the mince into a sausage shape. Use the foil to help roll the meat.

Ensure that the foil is securely wrapped over the meat before twisting the ends to seal the parcel. Place the parcel on a grid over medium heat coals or in the oven to cook for 20 â 30 minutes at 180Â°C or until the parcel is firm to the touch.

Remove the parcel from the braai or oven then remove the foil. If using the oven turn the heat up to 220Â°C. Place the uncovered bomb back over the grid (or the oven) and allow to crisp and caramelize for about another 10-15 minutes.
Allow the bomb to rest for 5 minutes before slicing into it and serving as a new braai alternative.

ing: extra virgin olive oil, for drizzling
salt and freshly ground black pepper
2 x 315 g Woolworths green pesto and bulgur wheat salad
st: Heat the oil high medium heat. Rub the spiced paste over the lamb to coat. Add the lamb to the pan and sear on both sides until medium-rare. Remove from the pan and allow to rest for 5 minutes before slicing.
Add the baby leaves to a serving platter. Spoon the bulgur wheat salad over. Add the sliced lamb and squeeze over the lemon and finish with extra seasoning and extra olive oil.

ing: 2 kiwis, peeled and cut into chunks
250 g strawberries, some cut into halves and some in quarters
st: Preheat the oven to 120Â°C. In a clean bowl, begin whipping the eggs using either an electric hand mixer or a whisk. Once the eggs whites become fluffy in texture add the corn flour and begin slowly adding the caster sugar and in stages.

Once the meringue has become thick and has a glossy sheen begin adding the brown sugar slow while continuing to whisk. Add the vanilla and cinnamon then whisk for another 2 minutes on a high speed once all the sugar has been added.

Prepare a baking tray lined with baking paper. Add large spoonfuls of the mixture to the baking paper before smoothing into a rough circle. Blob the remaining mixture over to create some height and texture to the Pavlova.
Place the Pavlova in the preheated oven to slowly bake for 50 minutes to an hour or until the outside is firm and the inside still a bit marshmallowy.
Switch off the oven and allow the Pavlova to cool inside the oven until completely cooled.
Spoon over all the lemon curd before topping with the fruit, sprinkle over the lemon zest and finish with a dusting of icing sugar.

ing: 5 cm piece fresh ginger, finely grated
st: Heat the oil over a high heat. Fry the garlic, ginger and chilli until cooked and slightly crisp. Add the sugar snap peas and stir-fry for 1 minute along with the spring onions.
Combine the soy, sweet chilli and BBQ sauce before adding and stirring through. Add the prawns and cauliflower rice before tossing until warmed through.
Serve in a large serving platter and scatter over a topping of spring onion, coriander and chilli.

ing: 180 g Woolworths crunchy veg with shredded chicken salad
st: Place the noodles into a bowl, then cover with boiling water and leave to soak for 5 minutes, before draining.
Place the cooked noodles into a bowl along with the crunchy veg and shredded chicken salad and the toasted sesame seeds.
In a bowl, whisk together the rice vinegar, honey, garlic, ginger, mint, coriander, chilli, sesame oil and fish sauce then pour over the salad and toss well.

ing: 150 g Woolworths French breakfast radishes, roughly chopped
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: Heat a griddle pan over a high heat and preheat the oven to 180Â°C. Coat the 4 thick-cut rib-eye steaks in the coffee rub. Use the following ingredients for the rub ( 2 tbsp finely ground coffee beans, 2 tbsp freshly ground black pepper, 2 tbsp treacle sugar, 1 tbsp smoked paprika, 1 tbsp ground chilli, 1 1/2 tbsp mustard powder, 1 tsp ground ginger, 1 tbsp salt)
Place the steaks on the griddle pan, fat side down, and cook until the fat is crisp. Turn and cook for no more than 1 minute on each side, or the rub will burn.
Place in the oven to cook for a further 6 minutes or until medium rare, depending on the thickness of the steaks.
Heat the canola oil in a saucepan. Slice the 6 sweet potatoes into 5 mm-thick slices, then slice into matchsticks. Coat with the 6 tbsp cornflour.
Deep-fry the chips until golden and crisp. Remove from the oil and drain on kitchen paper, then season with salt.

Serve with steak with the shoestring sweet potato fries, mushroom sauce and radish salad (150 g roughly chopped Woolworths French Breakfast radishes, 4 tbsp roughly chopped parsley, 4 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, 3 tbsp red wine vinegar and salt to taste).

ing: 4 cups fresh mixed berries (blueberries, raspberries, blackberries, gooseberries, strawberries)
1 cup cold coconut oil (the coconut oil should be set, not runny)
st: Line a deep square baking tin.
Mix together flour, almonds, coconut, sugar, baking powder and salt.
Using your fingers, rub in the coconut oil until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs.
Mix in the egg then press 2/3 of the dough into the baking tin.
Mix together the berries, icing sugar, corn flour, lemon juice and zest.
Scatter onto the pastry.
Crumble the remaining dough onto the berries.
Bake for 45 minutes at 180 until golden brown.
Leave to cool.
Cut into squares and store in the fridge.

ing: noodles, cooked, to serve with the stir-fry
salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 red chilli, seeded and thickly sliced
st: In a medium bowl, combine the soy sauce, chicken stock and cornstarch. Add the chicken and turn to coat.
Heat the oil in a wok or large skillet over moderately high heat. Add the onion, ginger and garlic and stir-fry for 30 seconds. Add the chicken and stir-fry for 5 minutes.
Add the chilli and continue stir-frying until the chicken is cooked through, about 3 minutes. Add the soy sauce and stir-fry for 30 seconds. Using a slotted spoon, transfer the chicken to a plate.
Add the orange juice to the wok and boil until slightly thickened, about 3 minutes.
Add the cabbage, tenderstem broccoli and peas to cook in the wok for 5 minutes before returning the chicken to the wok.
Add the papaya and stir-fry until hot, about 1 minute. Add the lemon juice, season with salt and pepper and transfer to a platter.
Serve with a nest of cooked noodles and spring onion.

ing: fresh lemon juice and extra to serve
1 red chilli, seeded and finely chopped
a generous pinch fresh thyme, leaves removed from stalk
a generous pinch oregano, roughly chopped
freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: Light your fire and burn it down until you have moderate coals.
Snap off the tough ends of 2 bunches of asparagus spears.
Coat the braai grid with olive oil and chargrill the asparagus for 5 to 10 minutes
Rub the cajun spice onto the flesh side of each kingklip fillet. Allow them to marinate for about 30 minutes. Remove from the heat and toss in olive oil, lemon juice and season to taste.
Make sure the 4 skinned kingklip portions are at room temperature. Splash a little oil onto the braai grid and place the fillets, skin-side down onto the grid.
Braai for up to 2 minutes, turn the fillets onto their flesh sides and braai for another 2 minutes. Remove from the heat and serve immediately with chargrilled asparagus and extra lemon wedges.

Place the eggs, white wine viengar, salt and a splash of water in a glass bowl and beat together before placing over a pot of barely simmering water and continuing to beat together for about 4 minutes until the mixture becomes thick, pale and fluffy in texture.
Remove the bowl from the heat and begin drizzling in the melted butter, a little bit at a time and in stages, beating vigorously.
Once all the butter has been beaten in the hollandise it should be thick and fluffy, season with a squeeze of lemon juice and salt and ground white pepper to taste.

Roll out the dough to a standard 35cm round circle before drizzling over extra virgin olive oil and adding the Italian herb mix Add the baby spinach and bacon before tearing pieces of mozzerella over.
Pour over a generous amount of the hollandaise before placing the breakfast pizza in the oven to bake at 200Â°C for 30 minutes.

Once the dough is perfectly cook and the hollandaise is slightly charred remove the pizza from the oven and top with the poached eggs and a few splashes of Tabasco sauce and some extra seasoning if needed beofor serving.
Generously coat the beef with the marinade and set aside for 30 minutes.
Heat a little sesame oil in a large wok over a high heat until smoking. Spread the meat out in the wok and brown. Remove from the wok.
Reduce the heat a little and add the remaining oil. Fry the red onion, pepper, cabbage and mushrooms until golden. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for a few seconds.
Add the remaining ingredients except the stock and cornflour. Add the beef and toss until glazed with the sauce.
Mix the stock and cornflour. Add to the wok and stir-fry for 1 minute.

ing: sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
500 g free-range chicken breasts, skin on
st: Preheat the oven to 210Â°C.

Moisten the Brussels sprouts, potatoes and chicken with the olive oil and season to taste. Arrange in a single layer â the chicken and potatoes skin-side up â on a large baking tray. Add the thyme.

Roast for 30 minutes, or until the sprouts are crusty and charred and all is tender. Remove the sprouts and chicken. Smash the potatoes and toss gently in the oil in the pan. Arrange cut side up and return to the hot oven for 5 to 10 minutes until golden and crusty.
Allow the chicken to rest for 10 minutes, then tear into large shreds. Mix everything with the dressing. Check the seasoning, turn onto a platter or bowl and add the watercress.

ing: sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
390 g pearl barley, rinsed and drained
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: SautÃ© the 12 chicken pieces in batches on both sides in the hot oil until deep brown. Remove from the pan and set aside. Season lightly.

Reduce the heat and add the 1 finely chopped onion to the pan. Cook gently until soft. Add the 1 crushed garlic clove  and vegetables (4 diced parsnips, 4 diced turnips, 4 diced kohrabi). Return the chicken to the pan, then add the 1 cup of stock and a few sprigs of thyme. Cover tightly and simmer for 30 minutes, or until the chicken is tender. Sprinkle with the parsley and serve with the barley pilaf.

To make the barley pilaf, soften the onion in the 2 tbsp oil. Add the 1 crushed garlic clove and 390 g rinsed and drained barley. Stir until lightly toasted. Pour in the 4 1/2 cups of stock, season to taste and bring to a simmer. Cover and cook for 35 minutes, or until the barley is tender and the liquid absorbed. Check the seasoning.

ing: 2 tsp fresh mint finely chopped, plus extra to garnish
st: 1 Fry the mince until brown and slightly crispy.
Add the garlic, lime zest and juice, fish and hoisin sauces and fry for a further 5 minutes.
Remove from the heat and add the mint and coriander. Serve with the lettuce, onion, beans and garnish with mint.
Using a slicer like a mandolin, thinly slice the beetroot into 1-2 mm slices and place in a bowl. (Wear gloves to do this as you donât want to be hosting your dinner with pink fingers!)
Combine the balsamic vinegar and the olive oil and coat the beetroot with it. Allow to marinate for about 10 minutes.
Choose a large elegant platter or individual plates and place the beetroot in a single layer on the plate.
Place the raspberries randomly on top of the beetroot.
Crumble the feta in about 1/2 cm nuggets and place it in between the raspberries.
Rinse and dry the basil leaves and plate them to stand up against the feta or the raspberries.
Use the left over balsamic marinate and dress the dish.
Finish with a crack of black pepper. (The feta has enough salt, no need to season the dish.)

ing: 1 red pepper, roasted and skin removed
40 g raw unsalted almonds, toasted and chopped
st: Combine the tomatoes, 1 tbsp. olive oil and garlic and allow to marinate for 10 minutes.
Roast the tomatoes for about 20 minutes in a hot oven until the tomatoes are soft, but still holding their shape.
Combine the crumbs with the roasting juices from the tomatoes and peppers and add the parsley and chopped lemon zest as well as the red wine vinegar.
Trim the stalky ends of the asparagus. It they are quite thick, steam them briefly before grilling, otherwise dress the asparagus with the 10 ml olive oil immediately.
Warm a griddle pan and grill the asparagus just before serving.
The asparagus should have some charring marks, but still be a bit crisp (al dente).
Plate the asparagus with tops to one end of the platter.
Place the peppers over the asparagus stems, top with the breadcrumb mixture and the almonds and garnish with the tomatoes.

ing: 350 g Woolworths medium fat cream cheese dollop with Chermoula, red peppers & almonds
1 cucumber, skin on and peeled into ribbons using a potato peeler
st: Line a loaf tin with cling film.
Lay the cucumber ribbons into the tin, making sure to overlap, also, leave some hanging over the edges.
Drizzle the asparagus with olive oil and season with salt and pepper.
Chargrill the asparagus in a very hot griddle pan then set aside to chill.
Mix together the cream cheese, feta cheese, chives, basil, salt and pepper.
Spread 1/3 of the cheese mixture into the loaf tin.
Layer Â½ of the asparagus onto the cheese, packing it as tightly as possible â this will ensure that your terrine cuts beautifully for serving.
Top with another layer of cheese, then top with the remaining asparagus.
Finally, spread over the final amount of cheese.
Fold in the overhanging cucumber ribbons to cover the top then cover with cling film.
Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes before unmoulding and slicing to serve.
Serve with crispy melba toast.

ing: 2 small red peppers, roasted, skinned and chopped
50 g fresh herbs (basil, coriander, parsley), chopped
2 cups quinoa, cooked in chicken stock
st: Combine all the ingredients  (15 ml sweet paprika, 2 cm fresh grated ginger, a large pinch of saffron, 1 grated onion, 15 ml ground cumin, 2 chopped garlic cloves, 5 chopped sprigs parsley, 10 chopped sprigs coriander, 40 ml olive oil, 1 juiced lemon and1 tsp of salt) for the marinade in a blender and blend to a fine puree.

To make the stuffing combine all of the ingredients( 2 cups quinoa cooked in chicken stock, 100 g dried chopped apricots, 50g chopped fresh herbs {basil, coriander, parsley} 1 juiced and zested lemon, 50 g toasted flaked almonds, 2 smallroasted skinned and choppedred peppers, a large pinch of cinamon and a pinch of salt) and set aside
To prepare the turkey remove any excessive fat, especially from the cavity. Also remove the gland on the parsonâs nose. Also remove the wishbone, if it is still in place.
Rinse the turkey and dry with paper towel.
Tuck the wingtips underneath the turkey to stabalize it.
Season the cavity of the turkey and add the stuffing. Pack it tightly.
Cross the legs of the turkey and tie the legs and parsonsâ nose tightly together with string to close the cavity of the turkey.
Season the turkey lightly and then rub the marinade all over. Make sure to use all the marinade.
Allow the turkey to marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 200Â°C. Place the turkey on a roasting tray and cover very lightly with foil to create a âtentâ around the turkey. Donât let the foil touch the turkey.

Place the turkey in the oven and cook for 1 and a half hours, then remove the foil and allow the turkey to cook uncovered for the rest of the time. You need to achieve a 70Â°C internal temperature when checking the temperature at the thickest part of the leg.
Allow the turkey to rest before carving.
Remove the stuffing for easier service and garnish with lemon and herbs.

ing: 50 g raw shelled pistachios, roasted and chopped
250 ml low fat plain Ayrshire yoghurt
st: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C.
Prepare a baking sheet â line it with baking paper and spray it with non-stick baking spray.
Combine the eggs, vanilla and castor sugar in the bowl of a stand mixer. Attach the whisk to the mixer and whisk the eggs to a light and fluffy consistency â to ribbon stage.
Melt the butter in the microwave and allow it to cool.
Sift the cake flour and then gently fold both flours into the egg mixture.
Fold the butter into the batter.
Pour the batter into the tray and spread evenly with a palate knife.
Bake the sponge for 10-20 minutes until golden and cooked.
Allow to cool then cut into rounds that will fit into the serving glasses. (It should not be thicker than Â½ cm)

Blend 100g of the raspberries with about 20ml water to a sauce consistency and brush the puree generously over the sponge bases to soak them. If you are a traditionalist, you can add the sherry instead of water to soak the sponges.

ing: 3/4 cup Woolworths medium fat cream cheese with chermoula, red pepper chutney and almonds
6 Woolworths jalapeno stuffing chillies, cut down the side, but not right through (just enough to create an opening)
st: Preheat oven to 200Â°C. Mix together all the ingredients for the filling (3/4 cup Woolworths cream cheese, 1/2 zested lemon, 1/2 cup finely grated mozzarella, 1 tsp smoked chilli flakes, 1 tsp smoked paprika and 4 tbsp roughly chopped coriander) ensuring all the ingredients are well combined.
Carefully spoon the filling into the 6 chillies using a teaspoon. Wrap each stuffed pepper with 2 slices of bacon before securing with a toothpick to ensure it doesnât unravel.
Place on a baking tray before brushing each bacon wrapped pepper with the 1/2 cup of maple syrup. Roast in the oven for 20 minutes or until golden brown and slightly crisp.
Serve with  1 cup of sweet chilli sauce spiked with 4 tbsp srirracha sauce as a dip for the poppers.

ing: 1 small cucumber cut into spaghetti strips with a julienne cutter
st: Combine the cucumber strips (discard the very dark strips), mint and strawberries in a glass jug.
Just before serving, top the jug up with ice and soda water.

ing: 150 g pumpkin purÃ©e (fresh chopped pumpkin, steamed then mashed to a smooth purÃ©e)
st: Grease a 12-hole muffin pan, and preheat the oven to 180C.
In a bowl, beat the 100 g butter with the 250 ml sugar until light and creamy.
Add the eggs, one at a time, and beat until well combined then stir in the 150 g pumpkin and 100 g dark, melted chocolate.
Sift together the 550 ml  flour,  45 ml cocoa and 7 1/2 ml baking powder then add to the creamed butter mixture, alternating with the buttermilk.
Spoon mixture into the prepared muffin pan then bake for 20-25 minutes until the cupcakes are risen and cooked through.
Allow to cool.

To make the frosting: Whisk together the 250 g softened butter and the 500 g icing sugar, 5 ml vanilla and spices in a mixer, until smooth, adding a splash of milk if the frosting is too thick. Colour the frosting using Orange colour
Place into a piping bag, then pipe onto the cooled cupcakes.
Using a pencil, draw 12 spider webs onto a piece of grease proof paper to make your decoration template.
Place the 200 g melted chocolate into a piping bag, then pipe the webs, using the drawn template as a guide. Leave the chocolate to set in the fridge until hard.
Place the webs onto the cupcakes, then top with a spider to complete decoration.

ing: 100 g Oak smoked Stanford full fat hard cheese, grated
st: Place flour and salt into a bowl, then rub in the butter until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs.
Mix in the polenta.
Add the egg yolks, then mix together to form a dough â if the mixture is too dry, add a little cold water until the pastry comes together into a ball.
Wrap pastry in cling film and leave to rest in the fridge for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 180ÂºC.
Roll the pastry out to 3mm thick. Then cut out 10cm circles.
Combine the filling ingredients and mix well, then place two spoonfuls of the mixture in the centre of each pastry round.
Brush the edge with beaten egg, then fold over to encase the filling and form a half-moon shape.
Crimp the edges to seal then place onto a greased baking tray.
Brush the tops with more egg wash, then sprinkle with sea salt flakes and chilli flakes.
Bake in the oven for 30 minutes or until the pastry is golden and crisp.
Serve with guacamole and sour cream to dip.

ing: 20 x 50 g Woolworths bulk assortment fruit jellies and gums
190 g Woolworths Royal icing mix: prepared as instructed
st: Cream the butter and sugar together until ale and fluffy. Sift together the cake flour and cocoa before mixing into the creamed butter mixture.
Turn the mixture out on a lightly floured surface before kneading together for a few seconds. Place in the fridge to rest for 30 minutes.
Remove from the fridge and let the dough soften until it can be managed and shaped. Roll out the dough to about 5mm- 1 cm before using various  cookie cut outs to press out shapes of the biscuits.
Place the cut outs on a greased baking sheet and bake for 15 minutes or until just set, they will harden as they cool.
Place the prepared royal icing in a piping bag, secure the end and snip off the tip. Use the icing as a glue to stick down the various gummy sweets, adding eyes and fangs to the biscuits.

To make the coffee ice cream, whisk all the ingredients (2 cups of cream, 1 cup of full cream milk, 130g of icing sugar, 1/2 cup espresso) until combined. Divide the mixture between 2 Ziploc bags, expel the air and seal. Lay the bags flat in the freezer and freeze for 2Â½ hours.
Break up the mixture and blend in a food processor for 2â3 minutes. Spoon into a loaf tin and freeze.

To make the hokey pokey, whisk the 100 g sugar and 4 tbsp honey in a saucepan over a medium heat until the sugar has dissolved. Cook until golden, then remove from the heat. Whisk in the1 1/2 tsp bicarbonate of soda and pour onto a silpat or silicone paper. Allow to cool and set.

To make the butterscotch sauce, heat the 2 tbsp butter, 100 g sugar and 150 g syrup in a saucepan over a medium heat. Boil for 5 minutes, then stir in the 1 tsp vanilla extract and 1/2 cup of cream. Cook until golden brown and sticky. Remove from the heat and allow to cool.

ing: 50 g cashew nuts, toasted and roughly chopped, to assemble
1/2 cucumber, sliced into ribbons, to assemble
90 g baby gem lettuce, to assemble
maldon salt and pepper, to taste
1/2 Woolworths rotisserie chicken, roughly shredded (bones and skin discarded)
st: SautÃ© onion in oil until translucent.
Add curry powder and tomato paste and cook for a minute.
Mix in chutney and water, then simmer for 5 minutes.
Remove from the heat, then mix in the shredded chicken, mayonnaise, yoghurt, coriander and season to taste.
Heat the wraps to soften, then fill with lettuce, cucumber, coronation chicken, nuts and fresh coriander.
Fold and roll to encase the filling, then slice into desired serving size.

ing: 400 g Woolworths fresh bolognese sauce, heated/prepared as instructed
4 x 70 g Woolworths hotdog buns, toasted
st: Wrap bacon around sausages & secure with skewers.
Place under grill and cook until bacon is crispy (about 5 minutes a side).
Warm up Bolognese sauce.
Finely chop red onion.
Roughly chop the parsley.
Grate the cheese.
Place the bacon-wrapped sausages in the buns.
Top with Bolognese sauce, red onion, cheddar and parsley.
Drizzle over Sirracha Sauce.

ing: 1 large egg white, at room temperature
1 1/2 cups Organic pinotage rosÃ© brut spumante, plus extra for serving
st: Place the sugar and Â½ cup water in a saucepan over a medium heat, and heat until the sugar has dissolved. Transfer to a bowl and leave to cool. When cool, stir in the lemon juice and sparkling wine. Freeze in an ice-cream maker, according to the manufacturerâs instructions.
When the mixture is half frozen, whisk the egg white until stiff peaks form and add to the ice-cream maker. Churn until it starts to set then transfer to an airtight container and freeze overnight.
To serve, scoop the sorbet into serving glasses and top with more sparkling wine.
Puree 6 hulled strawberries and halve 5 more, then transfer all to two teacups and top with sparkling wine for an indulgent summery cocktail.
Arrange your favourite store-bought rose-water Turkish delight with halved strawberries and serve as a sweet-and-light dessert.

Sieve 140 g flour with 65 g icing sugar. Rub in 135 g cold butter until the mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs. Add Â½ egg yolk and 1 t water to create a light dough. Roll, then cut into rounds and use to line individual muffin pans. Bake at 180Â°C for 5 minutes, or until golden.
Thinly slice 3 strawberries and arrange in the pastry shells. Top each with a dollop of double cream and serve as a moreish fruit tartlet.

ing: 600 g creamy courgette, bacon and feta soup, prepared as instructed
freshly ground black pepper to serve
Extra virgin olive oil, to drizzle over
100 g Woolworths barrel aged Greek style feta
35 g Woolworths spicy BBQ pork crackling
st: Add soup to a pot to heat up.
Ladle into serving bowls.
Top with lightly crushed pork crackling.
Roughly chop the parsley and sprinkle over the soup.
Using a microplane, finely shave the feta over.
Drizzle with olive oil.
Season with black pepper.
Serve.

t: Blue cheese and bacon beer bread
ing: 125 g streaky bacon, chopped and fried
st: Grease a loaf tin.
Mix flour and salt in a mixing bowl.
Stir in the beer and add a little water if the dough is to dry.
Mix in the blue cheese, cooked bacon, parsley and spring onions.
Transfer the dough to the loaf tin and bake for about 90 minutes.
Test with a skewer after about one hour when the top is golden brown - if the skewer comes out clean, remove from the oven and cool slightly before serving with butter and soup

t: Chicken pie with crunchy summer salad
ing: freshly ground black pepper, to taste
700 g garlic & herb potatoes, prepared as instructed
520 g Woolworths chicken pie, prepared as instructed
st: Prepare the potatoes as per instructions.
Place chicken pie in oven and bake until golden.
Combine the dill, caperberries, parsley, olive oil, honey and mustard.
Season.
Toss sauce through the potatoes.
Serve with Chicken Pie and Crunchy Salad.

ing: 250 g spring onion and chive cream cheese
st: Line a loaf tin with clingfilm, then arrange a layer of thinly sliced cooked multi-coloured beetroot at the bottom.
Combine 1 x 250 g tub Woolworths spring onion and chive cream cheese with 100 g chevin and season.
Spread a layer over the beetroot. Repeat until the tin is full. Chill to set.

ing: Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
st: Preheat the oven to 200Â°C. Rub the butter into the flour using your fingertips until it resembles breadcrumbs. Mix 1 cup cream and the lemon juice and add to the flour mixture. Combine the mixture well to form a dough, taking care not to overwork the pastry. Chill for 10 minutes.
Blend the asparagus and remaining cream in a food processor. Add the eggs and seasoning and mix well. Set aside.

Roll out the pastry to a thickness of 5 mm. Cut out 12 circles large enough to fit a Consol jar lid. Line the lids with greaseproof paper, then top with the pastry circles, weigh down with baking beans and bake for 10 minutes.
Remove the baking beans, pour the filling into the pastry cases and crumble over the blue cheese. Bake for 15 minutes, or until the pastry is golden, the filling is set and cheese melted.
Serve with the fried mushrooms.

ing: 1 Vanilla pod, split and seeds reserved
st: Place a small saucepan over a medium to low heat. Add the blueberries, spices and grenadine and bring to a gentle simmer.
Leave to bubble away until the berries become plump, absorbing all the flavours. Spoon over slabs of creamy Duetto and serve immediately.

ing: grain & lentil salad dressing (comes with the salad)
700 g Woolworths garlic and herb baby potatoes
st: Combine all the sauce ingredients into a pan, then simmer until the sugar melts.
Cook the schnitzels in the oven as per the cooking instructions.
Cook the potatoes as per the packet instructions.
Mix together the dressing ingredients then toss with the potatoes as well as grain and herb salad, then season to taste.
Place the salad onto each plate.
Dip the schnitzel into the sauce to coat both sides, then place on top of the salad to serve.

ing: 85 g Woolworths Belgian dark chocolate with cocoa nibs, finely chopped
st: Preheat oven to 180C, line baking sheets with baking paper and spray well with cooking spray.
Cream together the butter, sugar and vanilla until light and fluffy.
Add the eggs, one at a time, and mix well to combine.
Mix in the flour and chopped chocolate to form a firm dough. Divide dough into two, then wrap in cling wrap and chill for at least an hour.
Roll the dough out to 1cm thickness then cut out circles. Use a small star cutter to cut stars out of the centre of the circle cookies. (You can re-roll any extra dough to make more cookies)
Using a pestle and mortar, crush the butterscotch sweets into a course powder, then fill the star holes with the crushed sweets.
Bake the cookies for 10 â 15 minutes until the edges have just browned. Leave to cool on the tray for 5 minutes before transferring to a cooling rack to cool completely.

ing: 1 bag Woolworths Easy to juice red juice mix
st: Divide Woolworths red bag easy to juice equally into 3 or 4.
Place Â¼ of the red bag into a Nutri Bullet.
Add 2 tbsp rolled oats or quinoa.
Add 1/3 cup coconut milk and 2/3 cup of water.
Using the strongest blade, blend until smooth.
Garnish the rim of your glass with desiccated coconut and pour the smoothie in âfrostedâ glass.
Garnish with mint.

t: Chicken pie with Summer roast vegetables
ing: Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
1 Woolworths Spitzkoppe cabbage, cut into 4 large wedges
200 g baby beetroot, cut into quarters
st: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C. Coat the garlic bulb in some olive oil for wrapping in foil and placing in a roasting dish. Cut the carrots in half through the length and add to the roasting dish along with beetroot, kale leaves and the quatered cabbage.
Drizzle over more olive oil and toss to coat before adding the salt and freashly ground black pepper.

Place in the oven to roast for 40 minutes or until the vegetables begin to char slightly.  Remove from the oven and freshly grate a generous layer of parmesan cheese over. Return to the oven and roast for another 10 â 15 minutes or until the vegetables are perfectly cooked and the Parmesan is crisp.

ing: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: Only use tightly closed mussels. Rinse well and drain. Place the mussels, wine and garlic in a suitable saucepan. Cover tightly and cook over a high heat for a few minutes until all the mussels have opened. Discard any that do not open. Add the stock, lemon zest and juice.
Bring to a simmer. Add the cream and simmer for a few more minutes. Season with pepper â there should be no need for salt. Serve in bowls with the baguettes on the side, for dunking.
Slice the baguettes lengthways into sticks. Toast at 170Â°C for 10 minutes or until crisp and golden.

ing: Sea salt and freshly ground white pepper
st: Preheat the oven to 160Â°C. Season the chicken, then dust with flour.
Melt the butter in a deep roasting pan and gently fry the chicken until golden.
Set aside the chicken and fry the chorizo in the same pan for 3 minutes, then add the onion and fry gently until glazed.
Add the garlic and the peppers to the roasting dish. Pour the chicken stock and wine into the dish, stir and add the chicken and thyme sprigs.
Roast for 20 minutes, turn the vegetables and chicken, and roast for a further 20 minutes.
Turn the vegetables again and roast for a further 10 â20 minutes, or until the chicken is cooked through.
Serve with saffron-infused rice or sourdough bread.

ing: 2 Granny Smith apples, sliced into matchsticks
st: Spoon the cream cheese into a large serving dish or into individual dishes. Roughly chop the tomatoes and add to the dish. Add the avocado, apple, cucumber, chilli and salad onions.
Spoon the granadilla pulp into a mixing bowl, pour in the avocado oil and red wine vinegar and mix. Drizzle over the salad and garnish with basil, blackberries and edible flowers.
Season with salt before serving.

ing: 3 tbsp Verlaque fruit-infused balsamic reduction vinegar
st: Preheat oven to 180 Â°C.
Unwrap the camembert and place it in a shallow ovenproof serving dish on a baking sheet.
In a saucepan over a medium high heat, combine the butter and olive oil.
Add the onion and sautÃ© for 2 â 4 minutes or until it becomes translucent.
Add the berries and continue to stir for an additional 1 â 2 minutes.
Add the balsamic vinegar, honey, cinnamon stick, vanilla paste and thyme, stirring occasionally.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer for about 10 â 12 minutes or until the liquid has reduced to a jam-like consistency.
Remove from the heat and discard the cinnamon stick.
Pour the chutney on top of the camembert and top with the chopped walnuts.
Bake for 10 â 12 minutes.
Serve immediately with crusty bread or crackers.

ing: 1 tbsp fresh basil leaves, roughly chopped
1 tbsp fresh mint leaves, roughly chopped
3 tbsp blueberry, strawberry and blackcurrant preserve
st: Place the goatâs cheese in a bowl with the almonds and preserved ginger and mix until well combined.
In another bowl, mix the crushed ginger biscuits with the panko breadcrumbs, salt and pepper.
Transfer the crumb mixture to a shallow bowl or plate.
Roll the goatâs cheese mixture into equal bite-sized balls, dip each ball into the beaten egg and then into the crumb mixture. Coat the balls evenly on all sides.

Whisk all the ingredients (3 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, 3 tbsp blueberry, strawberry and blackcurrant preserve, 1 tbsp honey, 1/4 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp freshly ground black pepper) for the salad dressing together and set aside.
Heat a non-stick saucepan over a medium-high heat and warm the olive oil.
Add the coated goatâs cheese balls and cook for 1 â 2 minutes or until the coating is golden brown, the goatâs cheese is warm and starting to soften, but still holding its shape.
Carefully remove the goatâs cheese balls from the saucepan and transfer them to paper towels.
For the salad, toss the mixed greens and herbs with the salad dressing in a large bowl.
Divide the salad evenly between 4 plates or bowls, then top each salad with the goatâs cheese balls and fresh berries.
Serve immediately.

ing: Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
a small handful fresh Italian parsley
400 g sweet potatoes, cleaned, skin on and cut into thin wedges
400 g rainbow carrots, cleaned, skin and tops on
st: Preheat the oven to 180 Â°C.
Place the carrots and sweet potato wedges in a large roasting tray.
Drizzle with the olive oil, top with most of the parsley, season with salt and pepper and roast for 30 minutes.
Top the vegetables with the orange juice and zest, maple syrup and pecan nuts and roast for 10 minutes until caramelised.
Sprinkle with the rest of the chopped parsley and serve.

ing: Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
st: Heat the oven to 200 Â°C.
Rehydrate the porcini mushrooms in a cup of boiling water for 15 minutes or until soft, then drain the excess water.
Melt the butter in a pan and add the onion, porcini mushrooms, garlic, lemon juice and thyme. Cook for 3 â 4 minutes, remove the sprig of thyme and set aside to cool.
Spread a sheet of puff pastry with a layer of the farmhouse pÃ¢tÃ©, leaving a clear border around the edges.
Place two of the chicken breasts, overlapping each other, in the centre of the puff pastry and top with the mushroom mixture.
Place the other two chicken breasts on top of the two chicken breasts on the pastry.
Wet the edges of the pastry, then place a second sheet of pastry on top of the chicken breats and press the pastry edges together to close the parcel.
Glaze the pastry with the egg yolk, prick the parcel with a fork in several places and sprinkle with the black onion seeds (optional).
Bake in the oven on the middle shelf for 30 â 40 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Remove from the oven and serve immediately with vegetables of your choice.

t: Chai iced tea and coconut granita
ing: 500 ml chai flavoured rooibos brewed iced tea
st: Place the coconut milk, cinnamon stick, star anise and orange zest into a pot, then bring to the boil.
Remove from the heat, the leave to steep for 5 minutes.
Remove the spices, then stir in the condensed milk and brewed ice tea.
Pour into a rectangular freezer-safe dish, then freeze for at least 4 hours or until completely frozen.
Using a fork, scrape along the surface of the granite to make shards.
Serve in little cups topped with toasted coconut shavings.

ing: 2 cups passion & pineapple flavoured rooibos brewed iced tea
st: Place the iced tea in a pot over a medium heat. While the tea is heating soften the gelatin in cold water.
Add the softened gelatin to the tea and bring to a gentle simmer and stir until the gelatin has dissolved into the tea.
Divide the tea between 4 glasses before resting in the fridge at an angle for about 4 hours or until the tea has set to a jelly.
While the jelly is setting cut the pineapple into large chunks, coat in the sugar before adding to a pan and cooking until slightly charred. Remove from the pan and allow to cool.
Combine the yoghurt, vanilla seeds and maple syrup. Add the pineapple to the set jellies before topping with the flavoured yoghurts.

ing: a small handful fresh mint, finely chopped
st: Finely chop all the fresh herbs (30 g fresh mint, 15 g fresh parsley, 1 tbsp dried oregano), then combine with the rest of the ingredients (1 seeded and chopped chilli, 1 tbsp red wine vinegar, 1 big squeeze of lemon juice, 2 chopped anchovy fillets, 6 tbsp olive oil) and set aside for about 10 minutes.

Season the Rump and sear over hot coals fat side first (to crisp up) then the meaty side until golden and seared own all sides. Place in the oven at 180 then cook for another 20 minutes or until done to your liking. Slice thinly then toss the slices of rump in the chimichurri sauce. Serve with Haloumi Kebabs, Garlic Bread and Ready Made Green Salad.

ing: 150 g caster sugar, plus extra sugar to brulee
st: Heat the cream and vanilla seeds and the vanilla pod and bring to a gentle simmer.

In a separate bowl cream the egg yolks and sugar together using an electric hand mixer until pale an fluffy. Remove the vanilla pod and carefully add a little of the heated cream to the egg mixer and mix through tempering the egg mixer before adding the rest.
Return the mixture to the pot and bring to a simmer again before taking off the heat.
Add the berry mixture to a ovenproof glass dish. Before placing in a large oven dish filled with enough water to come halfeay up the sides of the brulee dish.
Carefully pour the brulee mixture over the berries and place in the oven to slowly cook at 150Â°C for 45 -55 minutes or until the outsides have just set but the center is a still a little wobbly.
Remove from the water and place in the fridge to set for 6 hours until perfectly set.
Coat the top of the set crÃ¨me with the extra caster sugar and burn with a blow torch until charred and set hard. Serve immediately.

ing: roasted and salted nuts, to serve
Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
st: For the salad blanch the 1 packet asparagus, 1 packet mange tout and1 packet tenderstem broccoli refresh in ice water and set aside.
Place the 2 nectarines (cut into wedges), 100 g rocket, 1/2 cup mint, 1/2 cup basil and extra parsley in a bowl.
Add the blanched asparagus, mange tout and broccoli mix to combine. Divide the salad between 4 serving plates.

Mix all the ingredients (2 tbsp finely grated lemon zest, 1/3 cup lemon juice, 1/4 cup olive oil, 1 tbsp honey, sea salt and crushed black pepper, 2 crushed garlic cloves, 1 cup of roughly chopped parsley) together for the dressing.
Spoon the herb and lemon dressing over the salad and serve with the lemon wedges.
Garnish salad with roasted and salted nuts.

ing: Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: Blanch the Brussels sprouts in boiling, salted water for 1Â½ minutes, drain and set aside.
Heat the butter and olive oil in a pan over a high heat. Toss the Brussels sprouts into the pan and cook for 2 minutes.
Season to taste and stir in the parsley and lemon juice.
Serve warm with a dollop of crÃ¨me fraÃ®che.

a: Adele Stiehler-van der Westhuizen for Prue Leith Chefs Academy
ing: 50 g raw unsalted shelled pistachio nuts, roasted and chopped
250 ml low fat plain Ayrshire yoghurt
st: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C.
Prepare a baking sheet â line it with baking paper and spray it with non-stick baking spray.
Combine the eggs, vanilla and castor sugar in the bowl of a stand mixer. Attach the whisk to the mixer and whisk the eggs to a light and fluffy consistency â to ribbon stage.
Melt the butter in the microwave and allow it to cool.
Sift the cake flour and then gently fold both flours into the egg mixture.
Fold the butter into the batter.
Pour the batter into the tray and spread evenly with a palate knife.
Bake the sponge for 10-20 minutes until golden and cooked.
Allow to cool then cut into rounds that will fit into the serving glasses. (It should not be thicker than Â½ cm)

Blend 100g of the raspberries with about 20ml water to a sauce consistency and brush the puree generously over the sponge bases to soak them. If you are a traditionalist, you can add the sherry instead of water to soak the sponges.

ing: 400 g Woolworths soetkoekies with condensed milk selection
4 Christmas chocolate brownie fruit mince pies
1 L Woolworths extremely creamy Madagascan vanilla ice cream
st: Divide the ice cream into 2 bowls. Roughly chop the chocolate and normal mince pies separately.
Stir the plain mince pies into the one portion of ice and the chocolate mince pies into the other. Return both ice creams to the freezer to set.
Once set scoop some of the ice onto one of the biscuits before sandwiching the ice cream.
Keep in the freezer until ready to serve at your festive table.

ing: 6 tbsp Italian Extra virgin olive oi
st: Preheat the oven to 190ÂºC
Very carefully cut your butternut in half. Remove and reserve the seeds. Cut each half into quarters and lay the pieces in a roasting tray.
Scrub, then quarter the beetroot and halve the smaller ones, then add to the tray. Peel and slice the onion into sixths and add to the other veg.
Remove the fronds from the fennel, popping them in cold water for later, then cut each bulb into 6 wedges and add to the tray. Drizzle with a little olive oil.
In a pestle and mortar pound the coriander seeds with a good pinch each of sea salt and black pepper. Sprinkle this over all the vegetables on the tray and toss to coat.
Roast the vegetables for about 40 minutes, shaking halfway through, until soft and golden and just starting to caramelise. Allow to cool slightly.
Meanwhile, make the dressing by combining the vinegar, extra virgin olive oil, mustard and seasoning in a small jug. Mix well.
Dress the roasted veg while still warm so they soak up all the dressing, then pick and sprinkle over the herb leaves, and reserved fennel tops.
Add the pomegranate rubies to the vegetables. Crumble over the feta, gently toss everything together.

ing: 500 ml M&S salted caramel ice cream
50 g hazelnuts, toasted and ground in a blender
st: To prepare the hazelnut meringues: Beat the egg whites until soft peak then add the lemon juice and continue to beat for another 2 minutes. Gradually add the sugar and icing sugar while continuing to beat until think peaks form.
Add the hazelnuts and combine into the mixture.

Preheat the oven to 120 and line a baking tray with silicone paper. Add large spoonfulâs of the meringue mixture to the baking tray then bake for 50 minutes to an hour or until the outside of the meringue has set. Switch off the oven and allow the meringues to cool inside until cold.

In a trifle bowl: Add some of the trifle to the dish. Crush some meringue over followed by some ice cream. Continue this process until all the ingredients are used. Top the dish with the caramel cream which is simply made by whipping the cream and caramel treat together.
Place in the fridge and allow to set for 3 hours. Remove from the freezer and allow to sit for 15 minutes before scooping and serving.
In a large frying pan, sautÃ© the leeks in a little olive oil and butter until softened.
Add the garlic, thyme and Brussels sprouts and stir to coat in the buttery oil.
Add the peas and cream and bring to the boil.
Season to taste and stir then transfer to an oven dish.
Mix together the breadcrumbs and cheese and sprinkle on top of the dish.
Bake in a 200C oven until the top is golden and bubbling.
Serve with the Woolworths Free Range Rosemary, Lemon & Garlic Partly Deboned Leg Of Lamb
Preheat oven to 180 degrees. Place the rusks in the oven proof dish side by side with the tops facing upwards so you see the bun pattern
Cube the apple into bite size chunks
Melt the butter in the pot
Add a dash of ground cinnamon and fry
Add the apple cubes and sautÃ© until apple has caramelised a bit
Remove the apple cubes and spoon into the any open grooves between the cinnarusk
In the same pot place the milk and cream and bring to boil
In the bowl whisk the eggs and sugar together
Add Â¼ milk and cream mixture to the bowl and mix well with the whisk
Add the rest of milk and cream mixture
Decant mix into a jug
Pour half the mixture onto the rusks and allow to stand for 15 minutes
Pour half of the remaining liquid mix and allow to stand for 5 minutes
Pour the last of the remaining liquid and allow to stand for 5 minutes
Place the dish in the oven and bake for 20-30 minutes at 180 degrees
Allow to stand for 10 minutes and serve with custard/vanilla ice-cream

ing: 6 fresh plums, quartered and pips removed
st: To make the plum sauce, place the water and sugar in a pan and heat gently.
Once the sugar has dissolved, turn up the heat and boil the mixture for 5 minutes until syrupy.
Add the plums and soya sauce, and simmer for another 3 â 4 minutes until the fruit softens and the juices are red.
Add the lime juice and set aside for the flavours to blend.
Preheat the oven to 220 Â°C.
Score the pork belly skin at 1 cm intervals and place it on a rack in a roasting pan, skin-side up.
Pour water into the roasting pan until just under the rack.
Rub the pork with the five-spice powder, lime zest and chilli flakes.
Place the pork in the oven and roast for 30 minutes or until the skin is crispy.
Reduce the oven heat to 180 Â°C and roast for a further 1 â 2 hours, topping up the roasting pan with water as needed.
Remove the pork from the oven and allow it to rest for 30 minutes.
Turn the pork, crackling-side down, onto a chopping board and cut into chunks with a serrated knife.
Serve the pork and crackling warm with the plum sauce.

ing: Woolworths exotic tomatoes, sliced and halved
handful Woolworths Edamame beans, blanched and podded
Half a block Haloumi cheese, sliced in half horizontally
2 Tbsp extra virgin olive oil, plus extra for drizzling
st: Layer a variety of sliced and halved Woolworths exotic tomatoes on a platter with peeled, sliced cucumber and Woolworths pickled red onion.
Scatter over pea shoots, olives, blanched fresh peas and blanched and podded Woolworths frozen edamame beans.
Slice a block of halloumi in half horizontally and fry on both sides in olive oil until golden.
Drizzle with lemon juice, extra virgin olive oil and season.
Eat while the cheese is hot and squeaky.

ing: 1 Avocado, cut in half with skin and stone removed
1 garlic clove, peeled and finely chopped
st: Blend all the ingredients in a food processor until smooth.
Transfer the avocado hummus to a bowl and cover with cling film.
Chill in the fridge for one hour.
Serve with warm flatbread, or use as a dip or spread.
Serve with a healthy salad or in a wrap, also delicious as a pasta or pizza sauce.

t: Crispy pork belly with plum glaze
ing: 6 fresh plums, quartered and pips removed
st: To make the plum sauce, place the water and sugar in a pan and heat gently.
Once the sugar has dissolved, turn up the heat and boil the mixture for 5 minutes until syrupy.
Add the plums and soya sauce, and simmer for another 3 â 4 minutes until the fruit softens and the juices are red.
Add the lime juice and set aside for the flavours to blend.
Preheat the oven to 220 Â°C.
Score the pork belly skin at 1 cm intervals and place it on a rack in a roasting pan, skin-side up.
Pour water into the roasting pan until just under the rack.
Rub the pork belly with the five-spice powder, lime zest and chilli flakes.
Place the pork belly in the oven and roast for 30 minutes or until the skin is crispy.
Reduce the oven heat to 180 Â°C and roast for a further 1 â 2 hours, topping up the roasting pan with water as needed.
Remove the pork from the oven and allow it to rest for 30 minutes.
Turn the pork, crackling-side down, onto a chopping board and cut into chunks with a serrated knife.
Serve the pork and crackling warm with the plum sauce.

t: Asian style crunchy stir fry wrap
ing: 1 cup woolworths easy to cook bright and crunchy stir fry mix, cooked
st: Toast the wrap and stuff with the leftover stir-fry, drizzle with the dressing, top with sliced rotisserie chicken and sprinkle with coriander.
Gently rinse, drain and dry the berries. Hull the strawberries.
Make the sugar syrup: bring sugar and water to the boil, then simmer for a few minutes until the sugar dissolves. Cool to room temperature. It will keep indefinitely in the refrigerator.
PurÃ©e the berries and mix well with the lemon juice, cold sugar syrup and alcohol (if using)
Freeze in an ice-cream machine to make a perfect, velvety smooth sorbet.
Serve in glass bowls to show off the rich colour.
Stir-fry mince in hot oil until crispy
Remove mince fry garlic, ginger, sesame seeds and sesame oil in the same pan for 1 minute
Stir in the sweet chilli sauce, soy sauce and basil
Add the mince and vegetable noodles
Stir-fry for another 2 minutes
Serve in bowls

ing: 250 g Woolworths spinach and cauliflower noodles
st: Cook the noodles according to the packet instructions
Place the olive oil, garlic and chilli into a large pan, then warm it up until it starts frying
Add the chicken, then stir-fry to brown and cook on high heat
Remove the chicken and set aside
Fry the tomatoes until they start to burst
Deglaze the pan with wine
Simmer over high heat to reduce.
Stir in the sugar, crÃ¨me fraiche and parsley
Season to taste and return the chicken to the pan
Add the noodles and toss well to coat in the sauce
Serve with a sprinkling of Parmesan cheese

t: Corn Dogs with Spicy Tomato Relish
ing: 1 cup milk (may need more or less)
st: For the corndogs, fill a wide, pan with 4cm depth of vegetable oil.
Combine the flour, polenta, sugar, salt and baking powder.
Mix together butter and egg then add to the dry ingredients.
Mix in enough milk to form a thick batter.
Skewer the Bockwurst onto the sticks then dip into the batter to coat.
Cook in hot oil until golden brown.
Make the relish by heating oil then add onions and sautÃ© until soft.
Add the paprika, cayenne, tomatoes and sugar.
Simmer gently until the sauce is thickened then stir in the parsley and season to taste.
In a large mixing bowl, combine polenta, cake flour, sugar, baking powder and salt
In a separate bowl whisk together one egg and the milk
Slowly pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients
Stir to combine into a thick batter

ing: 300 g baby marrow, cut into diaganol pieces
50 g pecorino cheese, freshly grated plus extra for garnish
500 g Woolworths Conchiglie Pasta, cooked as per the instructions
st: Halve some of the tomatoes while leaving the rest whole. Cut the onions into thin wedge like slices and add to a mixing bowl along withmarrow, tomatoes, garlic, rosemary, thyme, chilli flakes add the olive oil and toss to coat.

Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper before placing in the oven to roast for 35 -40 minutes at 180 until cooked and slightly charred. While still hot toss the olive pasta sauce through the roasted vegetables. Add the grated pecorino and stir through.
Toss with the cooked conchiglie and serve with an extra shaving of pecorino

t: Asparagus, sugar snap and mint risotto
st: Make the puree by melting butter in a saucepan, then add the asparagus, sugar snaps and water cover with a lid and cook for a few minutes until the vegetables soften, but still maintain their bright green colour. Place into a food processor or blender, then add cream and puree until smooth, season to taste, then set aside.
In a clean pan, SautÃ© onions in the olive oil until translucent.
Add garlic and risotto rice and stir over high heat for one minute.
Deglaze with the wine, then simmer until the wine is completely reduced.
Add stock, a little at a time, while continuously stirring â only add more stock once the liquid is reduced.
Once rice is tender, stir in the puree and parmesan, then season to taste.
Remove from the heat, stir in the blanched sugar snaps and asparagus, then serve garnished with parmesan shavings and micro herbs to garnish.

t: Apple and olive oil layer cake
ing: 80 g seedless white grapes, plus extra, oven-dried, to garnish (optional)
1 x 250 g cream cheese tub, at room temperature
st: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C.
Grease and line three 20 cm round cake tins, or use three 18 cm tins for a higher cake.
Place the grapes (leave them whole if they are small, halve them if they are large) and water in a saucepan and simmer over a low heat until the fruit becomes opaque. Strain and set aside.
Sift the flour, cinnamon, salt, baking powder and bicarbonate of soda into a mixing bowl.

In the bowl of an electric mixer, using the paddle attachment, beat the olive oil and sugar together, then add the vanilla essence. With the mixer on low speed, add the eggs, one at a time, until the mixture is smooth and thickens quite a bit.
Stir in the apple, grapes and lemon zest. Fold in the flour mixture. Donât be alarmed, the batter should be odd-looking â lumpy and fruity.
In a clean bowl, beat the egg whites until stiff peaks form using an electric mixer. Gently fold the egg whites into the cake batter.

Scoop the batter into the prepared tins, smooth the tops and bake for 30 to 40 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into the middle of the cakes comes out clean. Allow to cool completely before turning out.
Spread the maple syrup icing between the layers of cake, leaving the top un-iced. Dust the top with icing sugar and decorate with oven-dried grapes.

To make the maple syrup icing, use the paddle attachment of an electric mixer to beat together the butter and sugar until light in colour. Add the cream cheese and beat until the icing is smooth, then add the maple syrup and stir through.

ing: 100 g good quality dark chocolate, melted
2 ripe papayas, peeled, halved and seeded
st: Roll the walnuts into the melted chocolate and sprinkle with cinnamon.
Place in the fridge to set. Mix the coconut with the yoghurt and fill each papaya half with the mixture.
Scatter the chocolate-coated walnuts on top and serve
Preheat the oven to 200Â°C.
Grease 1 large baking pan or 4 smaller ones. Roll up the bacon rashers and place in the pan. Bake for 10 minutes. Add the sausage and bake for a further 5 minutes. Add the tomatoes.
Whisk the eggs until fluffy. Pour into the pan and reduce the heat to 160Â°C. Bake for 8 to 12 minutes, or until the egg is pale golden and just set.
Add a little black pepper and sprinkle with basil leaves. Season to taste with salt at the table.
Trim the crusts off the bread and cut into triangles. Place on a baking sheet and toast at 200Â°C for 15 minutes, or until crisp and golden. Serve with the omelette.
Chargrill the grapes in a dry pan over a medium heat
Add the white balsamic vinegar
Stir continuously until the vinegar has reduced
Remove the grapes from the heat and set aside
Toast the rye bread and spread with goat's cheese
Top with still warm grapes
Season with salt and cracked black pepper

ing: 1 small pumpkin, skinned and cut into slices
salt and freshly ground black pepper
1/2 small brocoli, cut into small pieces
st: Arrange the pumpkin wedges on a roasting tray
Coat with olive oil, paprika, cumin, coriander, cayenne pepper, salt and black pepper
Roast in the oven for 35 â 40 minutes until tender and charred

ing: salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
st: Cut the chicken into 8 portions and remove the skin
Add to a hot pan and brown on all sides
Once browned, remove from the pan
Place the same pan back on the heat then sautÃ© the onions until soft.
Add a splash of water to deglaze the pan
Stir through the spices and curry leaves and cook until fragrant
Return the browned chicken to the pan and toss to combine with the spices
Season to taste then add the milk
Roast in the oven for about 40 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the milk has reduced
Serve with steamed basmati rice and fresh coriander
Sign in/Register

ing: 3 x 40 g seed crackers & peanut butter dip
st: Line a mini-muffin tin with mini paper liners.
Place a teaspoon of the melted chocolate into each cup, then place in the fridge to set.
Place the seed crackers into a food processor and pulse until crumbled.
Add the peanut butter dips and honey, then pulse until well combined.
Spoon spoonfulls of mixture onto the set chocolate bases, then press down well until level.
Top with a teaspoonful of chocolate, then refrigerate again to set the chocolate.

ing: 1 x 75 g, punnet woolworths micro vegetables
5 potatoes, peeled and skins shallow-fried until crispy
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: Toss the vegetable leaves and micro vegetables.
To make the dressing, place all the ingredients into a blender and blitz for a few seconds. Pour over the salad.
Garnish with the fried potato skins and season to taste

ing: 4 large porcini mushrooms, torn or cut into large pieces
bunch kale, leaves removed from the stalk
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: Sign in/Register

ing: 500 ml vanilla ice cream, slightly softened
st: Cut up the cutie pies into chunks, then mix into the ice cream.
Return the ice cream to the freezer for 30 minutes to freeze until scoopable.
Scoop balls of ice cream, then place onto a tray, pressing down to flatten the underside of the ball. Place into the freezer and freeze for a few hours until completely set.
Melt the white chocolate and cream over a bain marie, then colour it red to look like a cutie pie wrapper.
Dip the ice cream into the chocolate, then place back onto the tray and return to the freezer.
When ready to serve, paint the top of each Italian Kiss with edible gold shimmer.

ing: 400 g brown mushrooms, broken into chunks
Â±1.5 kg woolworths sirloin steaks, cut into large cubes
st: Heat the olive oil over a medium heat. Add the mushrooms and allow to brown without being disturbed. After about 1 minute turn over to cook the other side. Add the garlic and rosemary and combine the ingredients.
Add the pepper and demi-glace followed by the cream. Reduce the cream slightly or to the desired thickness. Season with salt to taste.

ing: 600 g woolworths easy to cook chicken and tomato
st: Cook the chicken as per the packet instructions.
Place the tomato sauce, vinegar, Worcestershire sauce, brown sugar and water into a pan, then simmer until thick and the sugar is dissolved.
Slice the cooked chicken, then toss in the sauce together with the parsley.
Cut the rolls in half, spread with mayo, then pile on the chicken. Top with some summer salad for crunch.

ing: grated pumpin, enough to fill 3 cups
salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: Add the pumpkin and carrots to a blender and blend until coarse. Add the ginger and garlic as well as the salt, freshly ground black pepper, spring onions, herbs and coconut flour
Blend again to combine the ingredients then allow to rest for 5 minutes before molding into small patties.
Place the fritters on a baking sheet and cook in the oven for about 25-30 minutes or until golden on the outside and tender inside.Serve with wedges of lemon and rocket leaves.

ing: 250 g woolworths streaky bacon, crisped in the oven
salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: Slice the load open and spread the onion marmalade over the base before adding the crispy bacon. Add the sliced cheese then spread the mustard over.
Top with the chicken breasts that have been sliced before adding the top of the bread with the cut side up.
Prepare the cheese sauce by melting the butter then adding the flour, stir together for 30 seconds then start slowly adding the milk while whisking to prevent lumps.
Add the grated cheese and continue whisking until all the cheese has been melted into the sauce. Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste.
Pour the sauce over the bread and place in the oven to grill for 10 minutes

im: https://www.woolworths.co.za/images/elasticera/New_Site/Food/Content/Beef, cashew and broccoli noodle stir fry.jpg
ing: 2 x 200 g sirloin steaks, cut into strips
1 large onion, peeled cut into petals
1/4 cup woolworths easy to wok honey, soy & ginger stir fry sauce
woolworths easy to cook fresh egg noodles
st: Heat a large wok over high heat.
Add 1 Tbs coconut oil and allow to melt.
Massage the cornflour into the steak, then add to the hot wok and stir fry until meat is golden, remove from the pan and set aside.
Add more coconut oil to the wok, then add the onion and stir fry until beginning to brown on the edges.
Add the garlic, chilli and broccoli, then stir fry until the broccoli is tender â about 8 minutes.
Add the cashew nuts, then return the steak to the wok.
Add the sauce, then continue to stir fry until the sauce is heated through and coating the meat and vegetables.
Serve on egg noodles, topped with extra chilli and coriander

ing: 1 red onion, cut into thin petals
st: Remove the chicken from the bone before cutting into large chunks and setting aside.
On a clean chopping board: Begin arranging the vegetables as well as nuts ready for the wok. Combine all the ingredients for the sauce and set aside.
Heat the oil over a high heat. Add the chicken and let it sit for 30 seconds before begin to stir fry it in the wok by simply moving it around. Remove the cooked chicken.

Add the onions to the wok and stir for 30 seconds before beginning to layer the rest of the ingredients. Add the garlic, ginger, chilli, peppers, carrots, cabbage and spring onions while continuing to move the ingredients around the wok swiftly.
Return the chicken to the wok along with the sauce, toss to coat all the ingredients then add the noodles and toss through.
Add the cashews and coriander while giving the dish a final toss and serve piping hot.

ing: 1/2 cup extra virgin olive oil, plus extra for drizzling
240 g Woolworths hot smoked trout fillets
st: Place the cucumber and garlic in a blender and blend until smooth. Slowly drizzle in the olive oil in a slow steady stream with the blender running at a high speed. 2
Stir in the vinegar and season to taste with salt. Chill for 30 minutes.
Pour the soup into bowls and top with the trout, tomatoes and organic baby leaves. Drizzle with extra virgin olive oil.

ing: Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: Preheat the oven to 230ÂºC.
Drain the chopped tomato, reserving the juice. Turn onto a baking sheet lined with baking paper. Add the garlic then drizzle over the olive oil and season.
Roast for 15 to 20 minutes, or until starting to catch.
Blend with the reserved tomato juice and stock. Adjust the seasoning and refrigerate if you'd like to eat the soup cold.
Serve the soup topped with a spoonful of the marinated fresh tomato.

ing: 250 g brown mushrooms, some halved, others left whole
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
st: Preheat the oven to 200Â°C. Bake the schnitzels for 20 minutes until golden and crisp.
To make the mushroom sauce, fry the mushrooms in 1 T olive oil over a high heat until golden brown, about 5 minutes. Remove from the pan and reduce the heat.
In the same pan, soften the onion in the remaining olive oil. Add the garlic, thyme, cream and mushrooms. Simmer for 10 minutes, then season.
Serve warm with the schnitzels garnished with microherbs.
Marinate the steaks for 10 to 15 minutes.
Heat a heavy pan on the hob. Remove the steaks from the marinade (but reserve the marinade) and sear on each side for a few minutes until brown.
Mix the reserved marinade with the stock and add to the pan. Simmer for a few minutes â the steaks should be rare.
Remove from the heat, season with pepper, cover with foil and leave to rest for 5 minutes.
Serve the steaks and juices with steamed bok choi or broccoli moistened with sesame oil and sprinkled with sesame seeds.
Marinate the steaks for 10 to 15 minutes.
Heat a heavy pan on the hob. Remove the steaks from the marinade (but reserve the marinade) and sear on each side for a few minutes until brown.
Mix the reserved marinade with the stock and add to the pan. Simmer for a few minutes â the steaks should be rare.
Remove from the heat, season with pepper, cover with foil and leave to rest for 5 minutes.
Serve the steaks and juices with steamed bok choi or broccoli moistened with sesame oil and sprinkled with sesame seeds.

ing: 150 g Dried cranberry, cocoa & orange cookies, roughly broken
st: Add the coconut oil, cocoa and honey to a bowl and heat in the microwave until the ingredients are easily mixed together.
In a separate bowl combine the biscuits with almonds, coconut, sunflower seeds and pumpkin seeds.
Drizzle the coconut oil mixture over the granola ingredients before tossing together until well combined.
Place on a baking tray and place in the oven to roast at 180Â°C for 15 minutes. Allow to cool then store in a jar.

ing: 500 g Woolworths Prego peri-peri basting sauce
st: Preheat oven to 180C. Wrap the chicken drums with the bacon before securing with a toothpick. Place the chicken in a roasting tray before coating very well in the Peri Peri sauce.
Place the dish in the oven to roast for 20 minutes before turning over and cooking the other side for another 20 minutes or until the chicken is perfectly cooked and slightly charred.
Serve the chicken with the vegetables and cream cheese to cool down the heat of the peri peri sauce and of course Portuguese rolls

ing: 2 Golden Delicious apples, cored and cut into 8 wedges
st: Heat the olive oil in a pan, then add the sausages and fry until browned on all sides.
Remove sausages, then set aside.
In the same pan, add the sliced fennel along with the sugar, then saute until fennel is tender and beginning to brown.
Add the apples and a splash of wine, then simmer until the wine is completely reduced.
Add the cream and the mustard, then return the sausages to the pan and simmer for 10 minutes until the cream is reduced and slightly thickened.
Stir in the chopped parsley and season to taste with salt and pepper.
Serve on a bed of crushed potatoes or starch of your choice.

ing: 500 g Woolworths all butter puff pastry
st: Preheat oven to 180C. On a greased baking tray: Add one sheet of the puff pastry before adding the chakalaka and the Boerewors sprinkle over the grated cheese before covering and sealing with the second sheet of pastry.
Seal the ends by pressing them down with a fork. Place the pie in the oven to bake for 30 â 35 minutes or until the pastry is golden and puffed up.
Place the butternut in the oven and prepare as per the instructions.
Serve the pie with the filled butternut and the crunch salad
Preheat oven to 200C
Place the chicken into a roasting dish, then season with salt and pepper
Place the onion, lemon zest and juice, garlic, chilli, cayenne pepper, paprika, tomato paste, tomato juice and sugar into a blender, then blend until smooth.
Pour sauce onto the chicken, then place into the oven and roast for 45 minutes, turning frequently during cooking.
Thinly slice the potatoes then place into a bowl with the olive oil and thyme, then season with salt and pepper and toss well to coat.
Lay the potatoes out onto a large baking tray in a single layer, then dot the butter on top of the potatoes.
Place into the potatoes, then roast in the oven along with the chicken until golden and crispy around the edges.

ing: sea salt and feshly ground pepper
shavings of pecorino or italian parmesan
2 x 500 g rigatoni pasta, cooked as per instructions
st: Heat the canola oil. Add the beef and brown evenly for about 5 minutes per side. Cook the beef in batches instead of over crowding the pot. Set all the browned meat aside.

To the same pot add carrots, celery, onion and garlic. Cook until the vegetables are soft then add the tomato paste and Worcestershire sauce before cooking for 3 minutes before returning the meat to the pot, covering the meat with the sauce.

Cover the meat and ingredients with water before placing the lid on and slowly cooking the dish in the oven for about 1 hour to 1 hour and 30 minutes or until the meat is falling from the bone. Remove any bones from the dish before lightly shredding the meat.
Add the cooked and still warm rigatoni pasta to the hot beef and toss through the sauce.
Serve with fresh parsley a grating of Parmesan and extra salt and freshly ground black pepper.
Peel the onions, then cut in half across the equator.
Scoop out the centre od the onion, leaving about three layers of onionborder.
Mix together the cream cheese, cheddar, sweet chilli sauce, basil and salt and pepper then spoon into the hollowed out onion halves.
Put the filled onion halves back together, then wrap each onion in a double layer of foil.
Throw directly onto the coals  - the coals should be medium heat, and leave to cook for 20 minutes, turning often.
Serve with ribs or any other braai meat.

ing: 900 g Easy to cook free range beef frikkadels
130 g Carbclever cheese & onion seed crackers, pulsed in a blender till smooth
st: Preheat oven to 180C. Steam the cauliflower until completely tender and almost falling apart before adding to a blender with the cream cheese, salt and freshly ground black pepper. Blend to form a smooth sauce.
Drizzle the sauce over the frikkadel before seasoning lightly and topping with the baby spinach.
Pour the cauliflower sauce over the spinach before sprinkling the carbclever cracker sprinkle over.
Place in the oven to roast for 35-40 minutes or until the top is perfectly charred.

t: Beef koftas tzatziki pickled red onion
ing: 1 red onion, cut into thin petals
Woolworths heat and eat pita breads
st: Finely cube the cucumber before adding to a mixing bowl along with the garlic, mint, parsley and yoghurt. Stir together before seasoning with salt and freshly ground black pepper.
Heat the red wine vinegar along with the sugar and garlic. Bring to a simmer before adding the red onion and taking off the heat. Allow it to infuse while cooling in the pickle.

For the Koftas: Combine all the ingredients together then shape into a ball slightly larger than a golf ball. Skewer the ball with a skewer or kebab stick. Begin squeezing the ball down the skewer to form a sausage like shape.
Heat a griddle pan over a medium heat before adding the skewered meat. Cook for 2 minutes before turning slightly to cook the kofta evenly.
Squeeze the lemon over the kofta before serving with the pickled onions, tzatziki and pita breads.

t: Crumbed pork with sweet potato hash
ing: 3 cups orange flesh sweet potatom, peeled and diced into 1cm cubes
st: Cook the pork cutlets in the oven as per the packet instructions.
Heat olive oil and chilli flakes in a non-stick skillet or pan, then add the onion and sweet potato and saute over high heat until the sweet potato begins to brown around the edges.
Season with salt and pepper, then add the stock, cover with a lid and leave to steam for 5 minutes until the sweet potato is completely tender.
Add the spinach, then toss with the potatoes until wilted.
Serve the pork chops on a bed of hash then mix together the crÃ¨me fraiche, spring onion, seasoning, mustard and honey, then serve dolloped onto the pork.

t: Crumbed pork bacon sauce and mash
ing: 4 crumbed pork chops, prepared as per instructions
mashed potatoes, prepared as per instructions
50 g pecorino cheese, freshly grated plus extra for garnish
st: Heat the oil over a medium heat before adding the bacon to slowly cook until just about to start crisping. Add the garlic and cook for a minute then season with lots of pepper before adding the cream. Finish with the parmesan cheese stirred through before tasting and only seasoning with salt if needed.
Serve the sauce over the mash and crispy pork chops

ing: 180 g double cream Ayrshire coconut and lime yoghurt
1/4 cup CarbClever coconut and vanilla granola
st: Add some of the yoghurt to the bottom of a serving glass followed with some of the granola. Continue doing this until all the ingredients are used and layered.
In a separate bowl combine the coconut oil and the coconut chips along with the cocoa. Top the breakfast with the cocoa coated coconut along with the trio of fruit which have been halved.
Serve immediately or set in the fridge.

ing: 90 Woolworths small hollow milk chocolate easter eggs
st: To make the icing, cream the butter and icing sugar using an electric hand-mixer, slowly at first, gradually increasing the speed, until the mixture becomes light in colour and increases in volume, at least 5 minutes.
Slowly add the cocoa while beating. Once all the cocoa has been added, add the salt and milk, a little at a time.
Beat until the icing resembles the texture of chocolate mousse. Add a little more milk at a time if necessary.

To assemble the cake, stack the red velvet layer cakes on top of each other, sandwiching them with a little of the icing. Use the remaining icing to liberally cover the outside and top of the cake stack. Gently press the chocolate Easter eggs into the icing, starting from the base of the cake and working your way up. Top with a chocolate bunny.!

ing: 90 Woolworths small hollow milk chocolate easter eggs
st: To make the icing, cream the butter and icing sugar using an electric hand-mixer, slowly at first, gradually increasing the speed, until the mixture becomes light in colour and increases in volume, at least 5 minutes.
Slowly add the cocoa while beating. Once all the cocoa has been added, add the salt and milk, a little at a time.
Beat until the icing resembles the texture of chocolate mousse. Add a little more milk at a time if necessary.

To assemble the cake, stack the red velvet layer cakes on top of each other, sandwiching them with a little of the icing. Use the remaining icing to liberally cover the outside and top of the cake stack. Gently press the chocolate Easter eggs into the icing, starting from the base of the cake and working your way up. Top with Hugo bunny.

ing: 100 g leeks, washed and roughly chopped
1 cup Woolworths Ayshire full cream yoghurt
2 tsp Woolies Lazy Kettle Hickory Liquid Smoke
st: Heat the butter and olive oil in a non-stick pan over a medium heat
Add the leeks and fry until soft and translucent
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute
Add the spinach and fry until wilted.
Stir through the yoghurt and mint, then remove from the heat.
To make the chilli oil, heat the olive oil and spices until sizzling.
Add the liquid smoke.
Remove from the heat and fold in the yoghurt and spinach.
Season and serve with ciabatta.
Preheat the oven to 180C.
Line a square baking tin.
In a bowl, combine butter and chocolate, then melt gently.
Beat together castor sugar, eggs and vanilla until light and thickened.
Mix in chocolate mixture.
Mix together flour, espresso powder and salt then fold into the wet ingredients.
Roughly break up the biscuits, then add to the brownie mix.
Transfer the mixture into the prepared tin then dollop the caramel on top. Using a knife, swirl the caramel in the tin.
Bake in the oven for 30 minutes, or until the top starts to crack but the centre remains gooey.
Remove from the oven and leave to cool completely in the tin.
Once cool, cut into 8 squares.
Place the sugar in saucepan over a medium heat and whisk continuously until it has dissolved and caramelised.
Pour in the hazelnuts, gently stir to coat in the sugar, then pour onto a silicon mat to set.
Once cooled, place the hazelnut brittle in a food processor and blitz until it resembles a powder.
Melt and mix the milk chocolate with a hazelnut powder.
Roll tablespoons of the mixture into balls, place on a silicon mat and chill to set.
To make the glaze, melt the dark chocolate and mix it in a bowl with the flaked almonds and a pinch of salt. Using a fork, gently drag the hazelnut balls through the glaze mixture.
Place back onto the silicon mat and chill to set. Place back onto the silicon mat and chill to set.

ing: 4 tbsp fresh coriander leaves, roughly chopped
8  pieces Free range chicken drumsticks and thighs
