Drizzle some olive oil before seasoning with salt and freshly ground black pepper.

Over medium heat coals or on a medium heat griddle pan heat your kebabs. Grill without turning until the prawn begins to turn opaque and the cheese forms a crust, about 3 minutes. Turn them over and cook the other side for another 2 minutes or until the prawn is completely cooked through.
In a bowl, combine ingredients for the garlic and herb dressing.

While the second side is cooking brush your kebab with the herb oil, and once the second side has finished cooking give it a final brush of the herb oil and a few seconds of cooking just until the garlic becomes fragrant about 30 seconds.
Remove your kebab and finish with a squeeze of lemon before serving as the ultimate braai starter.

ing: Woolworths Peanut Butter Ice Cream, to serve
st: Place the butternuts directly into hot coals and allow to blacken all over. Add more ash and coals to cover. Cook in the coals for 30 minutes, or until a knife can be easily inserted. Once cooked, allow to cool. Halve lengthways and scoop out the seeds.

To make the peanut-and-chocolate crumble, place the white chocolate in a saucepan over a medium heat and melt slowly. Keep stirring until the chocolate begins to caramelise, scraping the bottom of the saucepan as you stir.
Allow to cool and mix through the peanuts. Sprinkle over some coarse salt and allow to set at room temperature.
To serve, scoop the butternut flesh into a bowl, top with some peanut butter ice cream and a generous helping of the peanut-and-chocolate crumble.

ing: 500 g free range chicken sausage, squeeze the filling out of the sausage casing
30 g fresh Italian parsley, roughly chopped
st: Sign in/Register

ing: 1 x 2 L ChucklesÂ® Malt Dairy Ice Cream
1 x 200 g pack triple chocolate chip biscuits (or any biscuits you prefer)
st: Scoop the ice cream into a large reusable ziplock bag. Squash all the ice cream to the bottom of the bag. Remove any excess air and seal the bag.
Roll the bag into a cylinder shape â the same size as the biscuits that youâre using. Wrap in clingfilm or tinfoil to hold the shape. Freeze overnight.
Slice a portion of the ice cream cylinder as needed. Squish the ChucklesÂ® ice-cream disc between your biscuits â and enjoy.

t: A modern take on apples and honey
ing: 3 Woolworths Extra Large Free Range Eggs
2 x 350 g Granny Smith Apples, peeled and grated
1 - 2 Granny Smith apples, peeled and thinly sliced
st: Preheat the oven to 170Â°C. Grease a 22 cm springform cake tin with non-stick baking spray or olive oil, then line with baking paper.
Pour boiling water over the sultanas, drain and place in a small saucepan. Pour over the brandy, bring to a simmer, then remove from the heat. Set aside to soak and cool.
Whisk the honey and oil until well combined, then whisk in the eggs one at a time. Add the almonds and whisk until smooth. Fold in the grated apple, soaked sultanas, lemon zest and juice.

Pour the batter into the prepared tin, smoothing the top. Bake for 50 minutes, or until golden and cooked through. Allow to cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then place on a wire rack to cool. Serve on a cake plate or stand.
Just before serving, top with peeled thinly sliced apple, painted with lemon juice and drizzled with honey.

ing: 2 - 3 sheets samoosa or phyllo pastry, cut into thin strips
st: vegetable oil, for frying
4-5 poppadoms
2-3 sheets samoosa or phyllo pastry, cut into thin strips
250 g shelled peanuts
100 g cashew nuts, roughly chopped
200 g coconut flakes
1 T fennel seeds
2 green chillies, sliced (adjust to taste)
125 g golden sultanas
8-10 curry leaves
1 tsp sugar
salt, to taste
1 t chilli powder (optional)

ing: agar agar powder (or 4 leaves of gelatine soaked in water for 5 minutes and squeezed dry)
slivered almonds, coloured with red and green food colouring, to garnish
silver or gold leaf, to garnish (optional)
st: 2 cups cream
125 g NestlÃ© Klim powdered milk
4 T rose water
1/2 cup condensed milk
1 tsp ground cardamom
2 tsp agar agar powder (or 4 leaves gelatine soaked in water for 5 minutes and squeezed dry)
30 g slivered almonds, coloured with red and green food colouring, to garnish
silver or gold leaf, to garnish (optional)

t: Brown Butter Prawns with Papaya Salad
ing: 500 g Woolworths Freshly Frozen Uncooked Extra Large Black Tiger Prawns, deveined
15 g Woolworths Fresh Coriander, roughly chopped
Woolworths Salt & Ground Black Pepper, to taste
st: Clean the prawns and set them aside.
Place the butter in a saucepan on high and whisk until the butter turns golden brown, about 5 minutes.
Remove the brown butter from heat and add ginger, garlic, and lime zest, and stir off heat until fragrant for 30 seconds.
Pour Â½ of the butter mixture over the prawns then skewer prawns onto lemongrass.
Grill prawns for 1 minute a side.
Toss the pawpaw, cucumber, red chilli, coriander and mint, finish off the salad with lime juice, and season to taste.
Serve the grilled prawns on a bed of the pawpaw salad and season to taste with salt and freshly ground black pepper.

ing: Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
2 cups of milk, extra if needed
2 T Woolworths Whole Chipotle Chillies in Adobo Sauce, chopped
2 x 75 g Woolworths Chicken & Herb Flavoured Quicksticks Noodles
Thinly sliced spring onion to garnish
1 T adobo sauce, reserved from the tin
st: For the chicken mince. Season the mince with salt, freshly ground black pepper and paprika, giving it a mix to combine well. Heat your oil in a pan over high heat. Add chunks of your mince to the pan and allow it to crisp before mixing in the pan, allowing a crust to form. Set the crispy mince aside.
For the cheese sauce, dust the cheese in the cornflour and add to a pot. Add the milk and place the pot over a medium heat allowing the mixture to slowly heat while stirring.
Once a smooth sauce is formed add the chipotle and adobo sauce mixing through to combine.
Prepare your noodles according to the package instructions but don't add the noodle seasoning to the noodles, instead and the sachet of seasoning to the cheese sauce and mix through.

Once your noodles are cooked strain off most of the water, adding the noodles to the pot of cheese sauce and combining. Divide the noodles between 2 serving bowls then top with the crispy mince and garnishing with freshly coriander and spring onion.
To finish combine some olive oil with adobo sauce and drizzle over the noodles and serve immediately.

ing: 115 g Lindt dark Chocolate, chopped and melted
3 T Woolworths Self Raising Wheat Flour
1 Lindor milk slab, a block for each centre
1 Woolworths Chuckles slab, chopped to serve
st: Set the air fryer on 185 CÂ°. Grease three 10 cm x 6 cm deep ramekins and dust with a coating of cocoa powder to ensure the edges do not stick and you get a beautiful even rise and bake.

Combine your melted chocolate and butter until glossy. In another bowl whisk together the eggs, sugar and vanilla until pale and fluffy. Add the flour and chocolate mixture with the salt and combine, do not over mix as this will result in a dense bake.
Divide the mixture between the 3 ramekins, place a block of Lindor milk chocolate into the centre of each pudding and bake for 8 minutes until just set.
Line the ramekins with a butter knife to release the sides and turn out your chocolate puddings, top with chopped chuckles slab and serve with double cream and fresh berries.

t: Chicken wings with spiced lettuce wedges
ing: 1 x 400 g can kidney beans, drained and rinsed
2 T Woolworths sliced pickled jalapeÃ±os, plus 2 T pickling liquid from the jar
Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: Preheat the oven to 200Â°C. Mix sriracha sauce with honey and soya sauce. Toss the free-range chicken wings in the marinade and set aside for 15 minutes.
Arrange 3 wings on 4 skewers, then bake on a tray for 45 minutes, or until sticky and cooked through.

Meanwhile, blanch the cobs of sweetcorn, drain and char over an open flame or on a hot griddle pan. Cut the kernels off the cobs and mix with drained and rinsed red kidney beans, jalapeÃ±os, pickling liquid from the jar and sliced spring onions. Season to taste.
Slice the gem lettuces in half, add a squeeze of Woolworths sriracha mayo and sprinkle with Woolworths fajita spice.
Serve the chicken wings with the spicy bean salsa and lettuce wedges.

ing: 200 g whole mini tomatoes (or halved larger ones)
1 fresh red chilli, finely chopped (seeded if you like)
st: 8 fresh tortilla wraps
Olive oil, for frying
Lettuce, finely shredded, for serving
For the filling:
125 g mature Cheddar, grated
125 g mozzarella, grated
100 g cream cheese
2 T thick mayonnaise
1 - 2 T coriander, chopped
300 g free-range rotisserie chicken, shredded
1â2 cup thick sour cream
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
For the tomato salsa, mix:
200 g whole mini Rosa tomatoes (or halved larger ones)
30 g salad onions, thinly sliced
1 fresh red chilli, finely chopped, (seeded if you like)
Red wine vinegar, a dash
Salt, to taste

Blitz the mushrooms with the broth, cream, flour and seasoning. Cook, stirring, until it boils and thickens slightly. Stir in the dill, chicken and lemon juice. Check the seasoning and allow to cool before using.
To assemble the pies, thaw the pastry slowly in the fridge so that it is still cold but easy enough to handle.

Place a sheet of pastry on a sheet of baking paper. Place 1 cup filling down the centre, then roll over to encase the filling. Do the same with the second sheet of pastry. Chill the pies while heating the oven to 190Â°C.

Slash the pastry diagonally, then brush with beaten egg. Bake for 25 minutes, or until bronzed and cooked through. Allow to stand for a few minutes then, using a sharp knife, slice each pie across into 2 or 3 portions, or many more for snack size. Serve hot with thick sour cream on the side, if you like. Itâs also good with a side salad of mixed leafy greens.
Cookâs note: Be generous with the filling â leftovers will, however, freeze well. Use in jaffles or snackwiches, adding some crumbled feta.

ing: sliced green and red chilli, to garnish
st: Sign in/Register
Heat 4 small mini cast-iron skillets on the braai. Add a splash of olive oil to each one and divide the paste between them. Fry until fragrant.
Divide the tomatoes between the 4 skillets and half-fill the empty cans with hot water or stock, divide between the skillets and simmer for 5â10 minutes.
Crack an egg into each skillet and cook for 5 minutes or until the whites are set. Carefully remove from the braai and cool slightly. Serve with the wraps, pickled onions and coriander.

Woolworths' new fresh pastes are the flavour bombs every home cook needs in their arsenal. Made with fresh ingredients, they add flavour to your dishes while minimising your time in the kitchen. These fresh pastes are inspired by flavours from around the world â laksa, sofrito, masala and harissa. Available in 150 g tubs.

ing: 600 g smokey cauliflower and shredded pork soup
st: Toss the cauliflower with the harissa and place in the basket of an air-fryer.
Spray with olive oil spray. Cook at 180Âº C for 15 minutes.
Fry the bacon until crispy. Serve the hot soup topped with the cauliflower and bacon.

t: Butternut soup with sorghum and amasi
st: Place the butternut in the basket of an air-fryer, spray with olive oil spray and cook at 180Âº C for 20 minutes.
Cook the sorghum according to package instructions.
Heat the soup, top with the butternut and sorghum and drizzle with maas.
Drain the cannellini beans and heat through in a saucepan. Stir through the pesto.
Heat the soup according to package instructions and add the beans. Serve with the Portuguese rolls, topped with melted mozzarella.

ing: poached trout with lemon and pepper
st: Roast the baby potatoes in an air-fryer for 15 minutes at 180Âº C. Crush slightly using a potato masher.
Heat the soup according to package instructions. Serve with the roast potatoes and poached trout.

ing: 340 g roasted red peppers in brine
400 g whole peeled tomatoes in tomato juice
280 g grilled artichokes with herbs in sunflower oil
245 g Pitted green olives with basil and garlic
st: Cook the pasta according to package instructions. Heat the olive oil in a pan and add the tomatoes. Heat through.
Toss the pasta with the peppers, artichokes and tomatoes. Add the olives.
Cook the pizza according to package instructions.
Add the garlic croutons to the Rosa tomato salad.

ing: 100 g sun-dried tomatoes, drained and chopped
400 g pasta of your choice, cooked and drained
st: Cook the garlic and butter in a frying pan until butter is melted.
Add the cream and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the salmon and sun-dried tomatoes.
Spoon over the pasta and season.

ing: 500 g Frozen mussels with garlic and herb butter
st: Cook the tagliatelle in salted boiling water for 10 minutes or until al dente, then drain.
While you are cooking the pasta, heat the olive oil in a saucepan and add the mussels. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir through the cream and serve on the past with a dollop of pesto. Season to taste.

t: Clem's brisket ragu with creamy polenta
ing: 1,3 kg Frozen beef brisket with dry rub, thawed
500 g French shallots, peeled and halved
2 400 g cans Whole Unpeeled Cherry Tomatoes
1 T parsley, roughly chopped, to garnish
100 g Italian Gorgonzola Semi Soft Medium Fat Cheese
st: Heat the oil in a large ovenproof saucepan or casserole over a medium heat. Add the brisket and slowly brown allowing an even dark, golden-brown crust to form. Turn over and brown the other side in the same manner. Remove the brisket and set aside to rest.
Add the shallots, bay leaves, carrots, leeks, rosemary, salt and pepper to the saucepan. Mix gently, then cook until lightly browned, about 10 minutes.
Add the garlic and tomatoes, setting aside the cans to rinse out when adding the water. Add the olives and oregano and mix, then add the brisket and just enough water to cover the ingredients.
Pre-heat the oven to 180Â° C. Half cover the pan with a lid, then cook in the oven for 3 hours. Remove the lid and return to the oven for another half an hour.

While the brisket is cooking, prepare the polenta. Heat the chicken stock in a saucepan over a medium heat until it just begins to bubble. Slowly pour in the polenta while whisking. Reduce the heat to low and continue whisking as the polenta begins to thicken.

After 5 minutes, swap the whisk for a silicone spatula or wooden spoon and gently stir every 5 minutes to ensure the polenta doesn't catch. Once thick, turn off the heat, add the roasted garlic and Gorgonzola, stir through then cover with a lid.
Before serving with the brisket, place the polenta over a low heat and add enough water to loosen, add the cheese in chunks and stir through the polenta until evenly melted.
Once the brisket is tender, remove it from the oven. Using tongs, break the brisket into large chunks and fold through the sauce.

Spoon the  polenta onto a large serving platter and add some of the sauce from the brisket. Add the chunks of brisket and spoon over the remaining sauce. Garnish with parsley, mint and the reserved celery leaves.

ing: 2 T Mediterranean extra virgin olive oil
250 g Free range lean beef mince
1 fresh bay leaf (use 2 if using dried)
180 ml Chilli and Garlic stir-through pasta sauce
500 g Rigatoni pasta, cooked al dente
st: Preheat the oven to 160Â° C. Heat the oil in a large cast-iron pan.
Add the mince and cook over a medium heat for 10 minutes until golden brown. Remove from the pan.

Add the onion and leeks and cook until soft and slightly golden. Add the meat and herbs, then add in two cans of water and simmer. Once the liquid has reduced by half, add the tomatoes, tomato paste and stock.
Cover tightly with foil or greaseproof paper and cover it with a lid. Bake for 1 hour. Stir through the fish sauce and the pasta sauce. Serve with the rigatoni and grated Parmesan.

ing: 1 to 1.25 cups water, this should resemble pancake batter
2 cups oil or ghee, for deep drying
ground almonds, mixed with 2 - 3 drops liquid food colouring or 1/8 tsp if using powder
st: To make the batter, place the gram flour in a measuring jug or bowl that you can easily pour from.
Gradually add the water to form a smooth batter, then add the food colouring. Whisk until you have a bright orange, smooth batter. Set aside.

To make the syrup, place the sugar and water in a saucepan over a medium-high heat. Bring to a boil. When the syrup is pulled apart between your index finger and thumb, it should have a threadlike consistency. Add the almond essence and elachi powder and set aside.

Heat the oil or ghee in a pan over a medium-high heat. Gradually pour in some batter through a perforated ladle, and fry for 1 minute. Remove using a slotted spoon, then drain on kitchen paper. You may need to change the paper towel a few times to keep them crisp. Continue this process until all the batter has been fried.

Add the boondi to the syrup and allow to stand to soak up the syrup for about an hour. Mix in the ground almonds. You can leave the mixture as is for a more rustic boondi or mash it with a fork to your desired consistency. I mashed mine with a fork. Shape into balls and serve.

ing: 350 g bulk raspberries plus extra for decorating
1 1/2 packets mini caramel swiss rolls, cut in half at an angle
500 ml Fresh custard with vanilla bean seeds
st: Place a layer of berries on the bottom of a trifle bowl.
Top with half of the prepared jelly.
Leave to set in the fridge. Layer the remaining berries on top and pour over the remaining jelly.
This will make sure all the berries don't sink to the bottom.
Chill until set.
Heat the oven to 110Â° C.
Beat the egg whites until foamy and gradually add in the caster sugar and beat until thick and glossy.
Spoon big blobs onto a lined baking tray.
Bake for 1 hour. Cool.
Place the swiss roll pieces on top of the jelly alternating with cut side.
Fold the cream into the custard and spoon on top.
Add the meringues.
Decorate with raspberries and chocolate almonds that have been rolled in gold edible shimmer

ing: 1 L fresh free range chicken stock
Purple spring onions, thinly sliced for serving
fresh ginger, 10 cm piece, sliced into matchsticks
st: Heat oil in a pan over a medium heat. Slice each chicken breast into 3 pieces and cook on both sides. Add the stock, bok choy and noodles and cook for 10 minutes.
Heat a pan over a medium heat and add the sesame seeds. Toss the seeds in the pan just until they darken slightly.

To serve, divide the noodles, bok choy and chicken between 4 bowls. Ladle over the chicken stock. Scatter over the toasted sesame seeds, spring onions, micro coriander, basil, mint, ginger and chilli.
